This led some orientalists to suppose a discrepancy and a contradiction in the words of God. But far be it from God that there should be any contradiction in His speech, because the summary is six and the detail is eight. When you find a summary and a detail, the detail is evidence for the summary, since these are overlapping days. How so?

They say: God created the earth in two days, then placed in it the firm mountains (rawasi), and blessed it, and ordained its sustenance within it. All of this concerns the earth. So when He says, ﴿in four days﴾, it means in the completion of four days.

Thus the total creation of the earth is in four days, and the first two days are included within the four days. It is like when you say, for example: "I travelled to Tanta in two hours, and to Alexandria in four hours," so the first two hours are included within the four.

Therefore, God created the earth with what is in it of firm mountains in four days. When we add two days for the creation of the heavens, the total is ﴿in six days﴾.

As for His words, ﴿And He revealed in each heaven its command﴾, it means He placed in it and ordained its affair within it. That is, He made clear its function and what it contains of good aspects, and who the messenger will be who will be in it, and so on, and He made clear its function upon which it stands in guiding the movement of life.

﴿And We adorned the lowest heaven with lamps﴾, which are the stars and planets that shine in the sky like lamps, including the sun and the moon. You will find that the light of the sun is different from the light of the moon. The light of the sun is called (ḍiyāʾ, brilliance), meaning light with heat. As for the moon, it has light only, which is why they call it the "gentle light" (al-nūr al-ḥalīm), because it is free of heat. Therefore the Most High said: ﴿It is He who made the sun a brilliance and the moon a light﴾ [Yunus: 5].

And He said: ﴿a lamp and a illuminating moon﴾ [al-Furqan: 61].

As for His words, ﴿And We adorned the lowest heaven with lamps and as a protection﴾, the lowest heaven is the heaven that we directly face and in which we see the stars. The lamp is fed by the light of the sun when it is reflected, giving a calm light that we call (gentle light), meaning that there is no heat in it.

The Truth, glory be to Him, who created creation and who knows best what sets it right, knew that there are two times for them: a time for toil and movement, and a time for rest and stillness. Night is for stillness and day is for movement. It is not possible to move with strength and right direction unless you have first obtained a calm sleep. Otherwise, whoever does not sleep and rest cannot work in the morning. But some activities happen only at night.

For this reason the Creator, glory be to Him, gave us a light that guides us in the darkness of night, like the (ūnāsa) as we say, so He does not leave us in darkness stumbling about, where the weaker among us is crushed or the stronger crushes us.

Therefore He said about the stars: ﴿and landmarks, and by the star they are guided﴾ [al-Nahl: 16]. The Truth, glory be to Him, made this to correct the movement of life, because God created the vicegerent Adam and commanded him to cultivate the earth, cultivating it with the matter and intellect God gave him, which chooses between alternatives, and with the limbs God gave him, which carry out the intentions of the intellect. So He, glory be to Him, wished to guarantee the safety of the universe along with himself. This is regarding the material.

The stars also have another function regarding values, before the mission of the Messenger of God.

And He said: ﴿and as a protection﴾, and in another place He said: ﴿and as a protection from every rebellious devil﴾ [al-Saffat: 7]. The jinn used to eavesdrop on the Higher Assembly (al-mala' al-a'la) in the heaven, taking some matters of creation that they heard from the angels, and descending with them to the soothsayers (kuhhan, sing. kahin), who would inform the people of them, claiming that they know the unseen. Indeed, some of these reports would come true, so people thought that they knew the unseen. A soothsayer would hit upon a true thing by chance, while along with it there were many lies.

This was before his mission, peace and blessings be upon him. But when our master, the Messenger of God, came, God protected the heaven from eavesdropping. Therefore He said: ﴿And we used to sit in it on listening posts; but whoever listens now will find for himself a flaming fire lying in wait﴾ [al-Jinn: 9].

For this reason we see that the Arabs used to resort to the soothsayers for judgment and believed them. It is narrated that Hind, the wife of Abu Sufyan, had been married to a man named al-Fakih ibn al-Mughira, who was one of the chiefs of Quraysh. His house was open to the people, and everyone in need of anything would come to it. They would say: "Go to al-Fakih," because his house was near the gathering place of the people.

One day Hind came down to attend to the affairs of her house, and found a man sleeping in the courtyard of the house, so she went back. At that moment al-Fakih entered and saw the sleeping man, and suspicion about his wife entered his heart. He said to her: "Go back to your father's house." So she went to her father Utba, and it became widely known among the Arabs that al-Fakih had accused his wife of such and such.

Her father Utba came and said to al-Fakih: "O Fakih, my daughter has been wronged, meaning she has been accused of something, and I see nothing for it but that we resort to the soothsayer to decide this matter for us. Gather from your men and your women whomever you wish, with my daughter in the middle of them, and we will go to the soothsayer and ask him."

Hind was an intelligent woman, so she said: "O father, you are going to a human being who errs and is right, and he may accuse me of something that is not in me, and then we will both be disgraced." He said to her: "Be assured. Your father is not foolish to this extent, and I will not present your matter to him unless he tells me the hidden thing that I have concealed for him." Before reaching the soothsayer, and he was riding a young mare, he dismounted in an open place and whistled to the mare, and the mare released the contents of its urinary passage. Utba opened the opening of the mare's passage and put in it a grain of wheat, then mounted her and went to the soothsayer.

Then he said to him: "I will not present my matter to you until you tell me the hidden thing that I have concealed for you." The soothsayer said to him: "A grain of wheat in the urethra of a mare." He said: "Repeat." He said: "A grain in the glans." So Utba informed him of the matter of his daughter, while she was in the middle of the women. The soothsayer went along, holding the heads of the women one after another, until he reached Hind and stopped at her. He did not speak to the others. At Hind he said to her: "Stand up, you are not barren, nor an adulteress, and you will bear a king named Mu'awiya."

These reports were true, and they were from eavesdropping, and they do not at all indicate the soothsayer's knowledge of the unseen. When Hind was cleared and raised her head among the people, al-Fakih wanted to make up with her, meaning: God pardons what has passed, and come let us go home. She said to him: "By God, the kingship of Mu'awiya has deceived you, and I will be most keen that it should come from someone other than you. Go away from me." After that she married Abu Sufyan and bore him Mu'awiya.

God put an end to this matter, because the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, could not be eavesdropped upon by a devil after his mission, peace and blessings be upon him. He said: ﴿And we used to sit in it on listening posts⦆ [al-Jinn: 9], meaning before the mission, ﴿but whoever listens now will find for himself a flaming fire lying in wait﴾ [al-Jinn: 9]. Thereby God protected the course of the heaven from being defiled by the desires of the devils.

﴿That is the decree of the Almighty, the All-Knowing﴾ [Fussilat: 12]. The Almighty is the One who cannot be overcome. As long as He cannot be overcome, no devil will be able to eavesdrop and take any news, and He, glory be to Him, is All-Knowing of the interests of creation.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 41, verse 13:

They turned away, that is, after all these signs, and after they themselves had acknowledged that He, glory be to Him, is their Creator and the Creator of the heavens and the earth. This is especially so since this is a matter that no one has claimed for himself. Since no one has claimed the act of creation, it has been left to Allah alone. Therefore, the Exalted said: ﴿Allah bears witness that there is no deity except Him...﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 18]. Allah bore witness to Himself and declared it. Did anyone object to it? No one objected.

﴿But if they turn away...﴾ [Fussilat: 13], after these clear signs, ﴿then say, "I have warned you of a thunderbolt like the thunderbolt of 'Ad and Thamud"﴾ [Fussilat: 13]. Warning (indhar) must be with something frightening and terrifying before it occurs, not after the thing warned of has happened, for a warning to be of use and for us to take precautions against it. If the terrifying event has already occurred, the warning is of no use.

Likewise, we have said regarding good tidings (bushra) of a pleasing matter before its time, so that we may welcome it. Thus, both good tidings and warning must each come before the event that is announced or warned of.

So say, O Muhammad, to those who denied Our signs: ﴿I have warned you of a thunderbolt like the thunderbolt of 'Ad and Thamud﴾ [Fussilat: 13]. "I have warned you" means that Allah, glory be to Him, is the Warner, and He, glory be to Him, is Mighty and cannot be overcome. Since He has warned of something, it must occur and be realized.

His saying: ﴿a thunderbolt like the thunderbolt of 'Ad and Thamud﴾ [Fussilat: 13] means: the matter is not merely words; it is a reality that has actually happened and has precedents, just as it happened to 'Ad and Thamud, and you have knowledge of them and see the traces of those people.

Here, 'Utba ibn Rabi'a, who was one of the chiefs of Quraysh, when 'Umar had embraced Islam and Hamza and al-'Abbas had embraced Islam, the leaders of disbelief said: "The affair of Muhammad is spreading. We must take action and determine our position regarding him to stop this spread. We should choose one of us who has wide knowledge of language and poetry, and a soothsayer skilled in the methods of soothsayers, and likewise a sorcerer; that is, someone skilled in everything with which we accuse Muhammad."

'Utba said: "I am the most knowledgeable of people in all of that, so let me go to Muhammad." When he went to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, he said to him: "O Muhammad, are you better, or your grandfather Hashim? Are you better, or your grandfather Qusayy? Are you better, or your grandfather 'Abd al-Muttalib? These did not revile us in our worship, so are you better than them, that you bring a new religion other than the religion of our fathers?

If you, O Muhammad, want wealth, we will gather wealth for you; if you want kingship, we will make you king over us and make you our lord; if you want marriage, we will marry you to the best of our women. And be silent about this affair which you call to, and desist from reviling our gods."

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said to him: "Do you hear?" He said: "Yes, I hear." So he recited to him from the beginning of Surah Fussilat until he reached: ﴿then say, "I have warned you of a thunderbolt like the thunderbolt of 'Ad and Thamud"﴾ [Fussilat: 13].

At that, 'Utba stood up and placed his hand over the mouth of the Messenger of Allah, and said: "I ask you by the ties of kinship not to complete what you have recited." Why? Because he knew that Muhammad does not say anything except that it comes to pass. After that, 'Utba withdrew from his people, until they said: "'Utba has become a Sabian (apostate); he has coveted what Muhammad has of good," meaning: he has become in need of what Muhammad has of wealth. 'Utba heard these words but did not respond.

After that, he said to them: "No, by Allah, I have not apostatized, but I feared for my people the warning of Muhammad of a thunderbolt that would strike them like the thunderbolt of 'Ad and Thamud, because I know that everything Muhammad says must come to pass. So I will save you from this by making him not complete this verse..." And the Messenger of Allah continued reciting the surah until the prostration.

When the Exalted, glory be to Him, gives a theoretical statement, He supports it with a reality, and Quraysh knew the story of 'Ad and Thamud. But what is the thunderbolt (sa'iqa)? The sa'iqa is that which strikes down whatever is beneath it. It may be a destructive wind, and it may come with a burning fire. The Qur'an said "sa'iqa," and called it a "sayha" (cry), and said: "a furious, violent wind" (rihan sarsaran 'atiya).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 41, verse 14:

His saying: ﴿There came to them the messengers...﴾ [Fussilat: 14] Thus in the plural, although the discussion concerns ʿAd and Thamud, and each of them had one messenger. So why did He say "the messengers" in the plural? They said: Because every messenger who comes is commanded by Allah to order his people to believe in the earlier messengers, and likewise to believe in those messengers who come after him. So it is as if ʿAd and Thamud, when they believe in their messenger, also believe in all the messengers. Or [the plural is used] because they were scattered across different places, such that each place had a particular messenger, and the number of messengers was multiplied by the number of places.

And His saying ﴿that you worship none but Allah...﴾ [Fussilat: 14] This is the summary of the call of all the messengers and the core matter of every messenger from Allah. ﴿They said: "If our Lord had willed, He would have sent down angels. Indeed, we disbelieve in what you have been sent with."﴾ [Fussilat: 14] Meaning: You are mere humans like us, and if Allah had wished to guide us, He would have sent us a messenger from among the angels. This is evidence of their foolishness, because the messenger comes as a conveyer of a method (manhaj) and a model of conduct (uswa suluk). If the messenger were an angel, the matter of being a model and an example (qudwa and uswa) would not be realized in him, and he could not command his people to do what he himself does, and his people would say to him: "How can we act, when you are an angel and we are humans?"

So the uswa here does not exist at all. Therefore, the messenger must be of the same kind as those to whom he is sent. Even if we brought him as an angel, as you wish, he would come to you in the form of a human, because you would not see him in his angelic form, and you would not be able to receive from him in that form. Therefore the Exalted said: ﴿And if We had made him an angel, We would have made him a man and We would have confused them as they are confused﴾ [al-An'am: 9], and the doubt would have remained as it is. Therefore, the messenger must be a man from the kind of his people.

As for their saying: ﴿Indeed, we disbelieve in what you have been sent with﴾ [Fussilat: 14], reflect: they acknowledge the messengership of the messengers and affirm it, and we want nothing more from you than that you acknowledge that they are sent, and it is strange after that that they disbelieve. They said: It is also possible that the meaning of ﴿Indeed, we disbelieve in what you have been sent with...﴾ [Fussilat: 14] is: as you yourselves say with your mouths, or "you have been sent" in the sense of mockery toward them, as in His saying about the hypocrites: ﴿Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of Allah...﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 7], and Pharaoh said: ﴿Indeed, your messenger who has been sent to you is a madman﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 27].

Madman? By Allah, you are the madman. For as long as he has been sent, why do you oppose him? So the whole matter is disbelief and obstinacy, and disbelief is madness itself: madness upon madness.

Then the Exalted wished to elaborate the account concerning ʿAd and Thamud, so He said, glorified is He:

﴿As for ʿAd, they were arrogant in the land...﴾.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 41, verse 15:

His saying, concerning 'Ad: ﴿So they waxed arrogant in the land without right...﴾ [Fussilat: 15]. Does this mean that there is an arrogance that is with right? They said: Yes. You act arrogantly among your people so that they will have a great one (kabir) who restrains them if they deviate, because the habit of people is that if they have no great one who is feared and to whom they return, their affairs become confused, they go astray in some matters, and they transgress.

This is arrogance with right, because it corrects the movement of individuals, and there must be a great one, as they say among us in the countryside: "He who has no great one, let him buy himself a great one." Why? So that affairs will be balanced and there will be no chaos. The poet said truly:

People cannot be set right in chaos without a leader (sarah) among them,
and there is no leader when their ignorant ones rule.

This is arrogance with right, because he has a standing (rasid) that permits him to be arrogant. As for arrogance without right, it is arrogance without standing and without a reason, like one who is arrogant through his strength, his authority, or other accidental attributes that are stripped away from a person.

﴿And they said: Who is stronger than us in strength?...﴾ [Fussilat: 15]. They lied in this as well, and their ignorance became evident, because God Most High is stronger than them in strength. ﴿Did they not see that God, who created them, is stronger than them in strength...?﴾ [Fussilat: 15]. Their saying ﴿Who is stronger than us in strength?﴾ is a rhetorical question of denial, meaning: no one is stronger than us, so he should command us and we should obey him, because we are the stronger.

Yes, you have a right in this, but what is your view that God who created you is stronger than you in strength? Is that not evidence of the obligation to obey Him? So logic required that you humble yourselves before the one whom God sent to you, and that you obey him as obedience to God who sent him.

Yes, it is not proper for the strong to submit to the obedience of the weak, but we ask you: are you stronger or is God? They must say God, because they acknowledge Him as Creator. So why did you oppose Him and clash with His messengers? You are indeed stronger over some of creation, but you are weak before He who created creation.

As for His saying: ﴿and they were denying Our signs [yajhadun]﴾ [Fussilat: 15], al-judud (denial) is rejecting a thing out of obstinacy and stubbornness, as God Most High said: ﴿And they denied them, though their souls were convinced of them, out of injustice and haughtiness...﴾ [al-Naml: 14]. So while they are certain of the signs and believe in them within themselves, they deny them outwardly. So what is the recompense?

The wind of punishment is described here as ṣarṣar, in two syllables (ṣar-ṣar), whereas there it is ṣirr, in one syllable. It is a violent, disturbing wind that threatens and carries intense cold, and cold by its nature brings about extreme dryness that dries things up to the point of burning.

The farmers know this phenomenon in winter, when the cold grows so severe that it burns the crops.

Thus Allah combines the action of fire with water, because the Truth, glory be to Him, did not create the universe as a fixed mechanical motion; rather He created it with the attribute of al-qayyūmiyyah (the Self-Subsisting Sustainer), which combines opposites. Have you not seen how, when Moses, peace be upon him, struck the water with his staff, every divided part became like a great mountain? Allah combined a thing with its opposite at one time. Likewise, when He struck the rock, twelve springs gushed forth from it. And in the story of our master Abraham, peace be upon him, when the people threw him into the fire, He made it for him coolness and safety, and suspended in it the law of burning.

So ṣirr is a violent, disturbing wind, but it blows only once; if it is repeated, it becomes ṣarṣar. ﴿In days of ill omen⁠﴾ [Fuṣṣilat: 16]. Naḥs (ill omen) is misfortune. When the day brings something evil, people regard it as unlucky. As He said elsewhere: ﴿seven nights and eight days, continuously⁠﴾ [al-Ḥāqqah: 7], meaning: decisive, uprooting them and bringing them to an end. That is, seven nights and eight days of decisive destruction, which settled the dispute between the messengers and the arrogant obstinate deniers.

In Arabic poetry a poet said:

Kindle the fire, for the night is a night of cold,
and the wind, O boy, is a cold wind.

So that the one passing by may see your fire;
if you bring a guest, then you are free.

﴿That He may make them taste the punishment of disgrace in the life of this world⁠﴾ [Fuṣṣilat: 16]. There is a punishment that causes pain, and a punishment that disgraces and humiliates the arrogant. Its purpose is not to inflict pain but humiliation, disgrace and abasement, because he was arrogant without any personal basis for it. Had We punished him with a painful punishment, he might have endured the pain; therefore We punish him with a punishment that disgraces him, rubs his nose in the dust, and demolishes his pride. Disgrace in disciplining the soul is stronger than pain felt by the senses.

It is well known that some people are hurt by mockery and ridicule more than by physical beating. This disgrace and humiliation is ﴿in the life of this world⁠﴾ [Fuṣṣilat: 16]. As for the Hereafter, it has another matter, more disgraceful, because disgrace in this world has a time at which it ends.

As for the Hereafter, it is lasting, permanent disgrace; he is punished and disgraced. ﴿And the punishment of the Hereafter is more disgraceful⁠﴾ [Fuṣṣilat: 16], because it is lasting and continuous. ﴿And they will not be helped⁠﴾ [Fuṣṣilat: 16], meaning: no one will take them by the hand, and nothing will save them from the punishment. They have no hope of help; they are not helped and they are not given respite.

Therefore we said regarding the gathering (al-ḥashr): Allah, glory be to Him, gathers all people at once, not in the form of a queue, for example, each waiting for his turn; rather they are gathered together, some with others, the oppressor and the oppressed, the follower and the followed. This cuts off the hope of the disbelievers for salvation, for they may have waited for their leaders to rescue them. Therefore, concerning Pharaoh, He said: ﴿He will lead his people⁠﴾ [Hūd: 98], meaning: he will go before them and precede them into the Fire.

Here is a pause for the theologians regarding: "As for Thamud, We guided them..." Guidance (al-huda) is indication toward the path of good that leads to a good end. We say: he guided him to the road. When you point people to the way, some of them listen to you and obey you, and some of them do not listen to you. The first, you increase in guidance and direction until he reaches his goal, while the other you leave alone.

Therefore the Exalted said: ﴿And those who accept guidance — He increases them in guidance and gives them their piety﴾ [Muhammad: 17], meaning: they accepted the guidance of indication. "He increases them in guidance": that is, with help and success in doing righteous deeds and disliking evil deeds. So there is guidance of indication, and guidance of success and help. And is help granted except to one who obeys you and believes in you?

We have previously given an example of this: the traffic policeman standing at a crossroads, when you need to ask him about the road you intend. He tells you: "The road is from here." If you thank him for his kindness and head toward the road he indicated to you, he increases you in guidance and explains to you the obstacles or difficulties on the road, and perhaps he accompanies you until you pass these hardships.

You asked him, he pointed you the way, you followed his indication and thanked him, and he said: "You are worthy of my help and guidance." But if you opposed his opinion and went on a different road other than the road of his indication, he will inevitably leave you, and leave you to yourself.

Likewise, the Exalted, Almighty, points everyone to the path of good; God has guided all creation. Whoever obeys in the guidance of indication is worthy of increase, and worthy of the guidance of help and success, while whoever disobeys and opposes in the guidance of indication is not worthy of the guidance of help.

Likewise was the case of Thamud: ﴿And as for Thamud, We guided them﴾, guidance of indication; ﴿but they preferred blindness over guidance﴾. That is: they preferred blindness to doing good, because they found ease in opposition and wanted to escape the bonds of the legal obligations. Otherwise, why did they worship idols while knowing what they are, and having made them with their own hands?

They worshipped them because in worshipping them there was satisfaction for the self, in having a god that one worships, and how pleasing it is for this god to have no obligations and no method of "do" and "do not." So, the hardship of the obligations of obedience and the sweetness of committing sin come from the obligation; if a god without obligations is found, the soul inclines to it and loves it, because that satisfies the instinct of the faith-based nature in man, namely that every human being affirmed the covenant at the first stage, the stage of the spirits: ﴿Am I not your Lord?﴾ [al-A'raf: 172].

So, the seed of faith is present in every human being from the covenant of the spirits, but people differ in accepting obligations and method. Among people is one who sees in the method a restriction on his desires, so he is not at ease with it and strives for a religiosity free of obligation, like those who "preferred blindness over guidance"; and among people is one who loves guidance and obedience, is at ease with the method, and feels intimacy with it.

Consider His saying: ﴿they preferred blindness﴾. "Istahabba" is not the same as "ahabba." Istahabba means: he forced himself to love it, and this is evidence that it is something not naturally loved at all, but they forced love for it to achieve their desire of lust. And you may consider any evil that God has forbidden you and suppose it befell you: would you love it? You do not love it; so it is not loved.

And in another place, when the Exalted spoke of the believers, He said of them: ﴿Those are upon guidance from their Lord﴾ [al-Baqarah: 5]. "Upon" (ʿalā) indicates elevation, as if they are seated upon guidance, as if it were a mount they ride that conveys them to their goal. Guidance did not come to burden you; it came to carry you and convey you to the goal of good. The believers are upon guidance, above it, which carries them; guidance is not above them, burdening them or obligating them with what they cannot bear. So guidance is a service to you and for your benefit...

Then He, glorified, says: ﴿So the thunderbolt of the humiliating punishment seized them for what they used to earn﴾. We said earlier: the thunderbolt (ṣāʿiqa) is everything that strikes and destroys, whether by wind or fire, or a destroying cry. The humiliating punishment (al-ʿadhāb al-hawn) means: accompanied by disgrace and shame. ﴿For what they used to earn﴾ means: this happened to them because of what they earned, and what their hands had committed. That is: a fitting recompense, not injustice and aggression.

It is frequently found that the style of the Noble Qur'an combines a thing with its opposite in order to bring out the meaning, for things are distinguished by their contraries. Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿Indeed, the righteous will be in bliss. And indeed, the wicked will be in the Blazing Fire﴾ [al-Infitar: 13-14]. This is an antithesis in which each meaning clarifies the opposite meaning. Likewise here, after the True One (al-Haqq), glory be to Him, related to us concerning some of the obstinate deniers, He followed that with speech about the believers, the pious, and what they came to of success and deliverance. So He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿And We saved those who believed and used to be mindful of Allah﴾ [Fussilat: 18].

Allah will certainly gather them all at one time, with their leaders and the heads of disbelief going before them. ﴿Then We will surely drag out from every sect those of them who were most insolent against the Most Merciful﴾ [Maryam: 69]. That is, We will bring forward the strongmen and send them to the Fire before the weak. It is as if Allah is saying to them: "These are your leaders, and they will reach the Fire ahead of you. The wild beasts (al-wuhush) are the animals that are not tamed, such as the lion, the panther, and others. It is as if the Truth, glorified is He, wants to say to us: "I am the One who subdues creation for you. If I had not subdued it for you, you would not have been able to subdue it." Indeed, He subdued the camel for you despite its great size, but He did not subdue for you the small serpent. ﴿Do they not see that We created for them, from what Our hands have made, grazing livestock, and they are their owners? And We subjected them to them, so some of them they ride and some of them they eat﴾ [Ya-Sin: 71–72].

By Allah, if Allah had not subdued these creatures for us, we would have gained nothing from them. Therefore we say of what is not subdued: it is a wild animal. Do you not see a child or a small boy leading a large camel, loading it, making it kneel, and driving it wherever he wants? Yet a small flea in the bed disturbs you and prevents you from sleeping. It is a message from the Creator, glorified is He, that the matter is one of subjection from Allah.

﴿And on the Day the enemies of Allah are gathered to the Fire, they will be driven in groups﴾ [Fussilat: 19]. In this world the wild beasts flee from man, and we flee from the wild beasts. But on the Day of Resurrection, Allah will gather everyone together in one place. How? Because none of us will have any power to act. ﴿Whose is the dominion today? It is for Allah, the One, the Subduer﴾ [Ghafir: 16]. When the dominion belongs to Allah, there will remain among us, the created beings, no difference in strength by which one could be overpowered.

His saying ﴿so they will be driven in groups﴾ [Fussilat: 19] means that they will be driven and led altogether to the Fire, from the first of them to the last. ﴿Until, when they reach it, their hearing, their sight, and their skins will testify against them as to what they used to do﴾ [Fussilat: 20].

Yet the Truth mentions only three of them here: hearing, sight, and skins. He does not mention the hand or the nose.

It has been said: this is because the obligation concerning the nose is rare and limited, such as when you smell wine, God forbid, or smell a woman wearing perfume. So the nose has a limited role. As for hearing, it is the most important of the senses, because through it you receive the call to Allah. And sight is what you use to perceive the signs of Allah in His universe and the wonders of His creation.

As for the skins, they encompass hearing, sight, and all the senses. It is as if the skin is the most general thing in sensation. For this reason, when they researched the functions of the organs to know the importance of each organ in the human being, they found that the most important of them is the skin, because it is the means of feeling pain, especially in its outer layer. Do you not see that when you receive an injection, you feel the pain of the needle as it enters your body and pierces the skin? It hurts you according to the extent of its penetration into the skin, as if the skin is the place of tasting. Since it is the place of tasting, it therefore encompasses all the senses.

For this reason the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿Every time their skins are roasted through, We will substitute for them other skins that they may taste the punishment…﴾ [al-Nisa: 56]. So the skin is the place where the punishment is tasted, God forbid, and it is the one that encompasses all the senses.

Had they answered the question, "Why did you testify against us?", they would have said: "We testified against you because we are the strongest guardian over you at all times." ﴿They said: "God has made us speak, He who made everything speak..."﴾ [Fussilat: 21]. That is: the matter is not in our hands; we did not testify of our own accord. Rather, the Truth made us speak with the truth, and we have no way out of this.

The meaning of ﴿He who made everything speak...﴾ [Fussilat: 21] is that everything in existence has its own particular language, a language by which it speaks, a language that conveys meaning and can be understood. We see this in the story of Prophet Sulayman (peace be upon him), when an ant spoke and warned her people, saying: ﴿Enter your dwellings, lest Sulayman and his hosts crush you while they do not perceive﴾ [al-Naml: 18].

The ant's words show that ants have a language by which they understand one another, and they show her alertness and her justice in judgment when she said: ﴿while they do not perceive﴾ [al-Naml: 18].

So too the account of the hoopoe in the same story, when he said: ﴿I have encompassed what you have not encompassed, and I have brought you certain news from Saba﴾ [al-Naml: 22], and then spoke words at the very core of belief: ﴿I found her and her people prostrating to the sun instead of God...﴾ [al-Naml: 24]. The hoopoe was therefore not merely one who speaks a language; he understood the most important matters of faith and the questions of monotheism.

Thus: everything has a language, but none knows it except the one whom God has taught and granted knowledge of that language. This is the bounty of God, which He gives to whom He wills. For this reason Prophet Sulayman said: ﴿We have been taught the speech of birds...﴾ [al-Naml: 16], and had God not taught him, he would not have understood the hoopoe.

Likewise, inanimate matter has a language, as God says: ﴿We subjected the mountains to glorify [Us] with him, at evening and at sunrise﴾ [Sad: 18].

Therefore God states this matter in summary: ﴿There is not a thing but glorifies Him with His praise, but you do not understand their glorification...﴾ [al-Isra: 44].

It is reported that pebbles glorified God in the hand of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and this is one of his miracles (ﷺ). In correcting this matter we have said: the pebble glorifies God in the hand of the Messenger of God just as it glorifies Him in the hand of Abu Jahl. The correct and miraculous statement is that the Messenger of God heard the glorification of the pebbles in his hand; this is how the matter should be phrased.

Some scholars say that this glorification is a glorification indicating its Creator, not a glorification in reality. This statement contradicts the text of the Noble Qur'an, for if it were a glorification merely indicating its Creator, as you say, then you would have understood it, and God says: ﴿but you do not understand their glorification...﴾ [al-Isra: 44]. Therefore it is a glorification in reality, a glorification in a language known only to its Creator, or to the one whom God has taught and singled out with an abundance of His bounty.

What is remarkable in the matter of the hoopoe is that he mentioned only one reason for the obligation to believe in God and to affirm His oneness, saying: ﴿that they should not prostrate to God, who brings forth what is hidden in the heavens and the earth, and knows what you conceal and what you disclose﴾ [al-Naml: 25]. He mentioned the matter specific to him, namely bringing forth the hidden things of the earth, and it is well known that the hoopoe has a long beak with which he pulls worms from beneath the surface of the soil and feeds on them.

As for His saying: ﴿And He created you the first time, and to Him you will be returned﴾ [Fussilat: 21], the meaning is: do not think that God created you and left you neglected. Rather, He created you for a purpose, and you will certainly return to Him and stand before Him, and He will call you to account for the smallest and the greatest, and recompense you for your deeds. You will not escape from Him, glory be to Him. You will stand before Him for reckoning; He will enumerate His blessings upon you, and He will see who gave thanks for them and who disbelieved.

Meaning: there is something important you have overlooked and did not notice: you used to conceal yourselves from creation so that no one would see you while committing sin, yet you forgot that Allah is watching you, sees you, and observes your actions. Nor did you conceal yourselves from your own selves and your limbs, and it escaped your notice that the limbs will bear witness against you on the Day of Resurrection.

So the hand with which you struck, the foot with which you walked, the tongue, the ear and the eye, all the limbs, will come bearing witness against you on the Day of Resurrection. These limbs, which Allah commanded to be subject to your desires in this world and to obey you in everything you want, will be freed from this bondage on the Day of Resurrection, so you will have no authority over them, and at that time they will testify against you.

If they obeyed you in sins in this world, because Allah subjected them to you, then they obeyed you while hating your act and being innocent of it. But now that everything has returned to Allah, and the dominion is entirely His, ﴿Whose is the dominion this Day? It is Allah's, the One, the Subduer﴾ [Ghafir: 16], there is no wonder, then, that your limbs bear witness against you and become adversaries to you before their Creator, may He be exalted.

We have previously illustrated this matter with the commander of a battalion in an army who orders his soldiers, and they carry out his orders, executing the commands even if they are mistaken. Then, when they come before the supreme commander, they complain to him of the injustice of their immediate commander, saying: he did such-and-such to us.

Likewise, a person's limbs have been commanded by Allah to obey him, even in disobedience, and to be subject to his desires. So your limbs obey you in everything you want, in good and in evil.

As for His saying: ﴿But you thought that Allah does not know much of what you do﴾ [Fussilat: 22], the Truthful, Glorified and Exalted says in a sacred hadith: "If you cannot do to a human being like yourself a deed that would displease him in his sight and hearing, [then] by My eye, [so] how would you do it in the presence of Allah, may He be exalted?"

And that is your assumption which you assumed about your Lord; it destroyed you, and you became among the losers.

Here is the translation of the passage:

"His saying: ﴿And that...﴾ [Fussilat: 23] means: your deeds that you did. ﴿Your assumption which you assumed about your Lord...﴾ [Fussilat: 23] means: you assumed that He, glory be to Him, does not know what you do. ﴿It destroyed you...﴾ [Fussilat: 23] means: this assumption brought you to ruin. ﴿So you became among the losers﴾ [Fussilat: 23]."

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 41, verse 24:

That is: if they endure what they are upon, and persist in disbelief and in disputing with the Messengers, what will happen? ﴿Then the Fire is their abode.﴾ ﴿And if they seek to be reconciled, they will not be among those who are reconciled.﴾ It is a matter of two alternatives. When a person opposes the commands of his Creator, and a Messenger comes to him saying, "Do not do this," then if he desists, it is better for him; and if he persists and perseveres in it, then the Fire is his abode.

The meaning of ﴿yastaʿtibūn﴾ (they seek to be reconciled) and ﴿mina l-muʿtabīn﴾ (among those who are reconciled): "yastaʿtibūn" means they seek al-ʿutbā (reconciliation, the removal of blame). It is said: ʿatiba fulān ʿalā fulān, meaning he blamed him for a matter that should not have come from him. For example, if I am ill and you do not visit me, this is ʿitāb (reproach), and you say, "I apologize, for I was busy with such and such." Then, when he explains the excuse to him, he has ʿaʿtabahu, meaning he removed his reproach. This will not happen for them in the Hereafter; if they seek reproach, they will not be reconciled.

Therefore, it came in the hadith of the Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, when he was returning from al-Ta'if after its people had harmed him, that he said, among what he said while communing with his Lord, "To You is the reproach until You are pleased." That is: if anything has proceeded from me that displeases You, then I remove it, and I acknowledge that I am weak, seeking acceptance of the reproach...

So: you do not reproach anyone except when you love the one you reproach and are eager for your relationship with him. We say: "ʿatabtu ʿalayhi fa-aʿtabanī," meaning he removed my reproach. As for these people in the Hereafter, Allah will not accept reproach from them, and will not remove their blame. The hamzah in aʿtaba is called hamzat al-izāla (the hamzah of removal)...

Meaning of "wa-qayyadna lahum": that is, We prepared for them and appointed for them companions (qurana'), associates who would cling to them. The root meaning of al-muqayada (exchange) in buying and selling is like when you pay the price and take the goods. For God, Exalted, wants the servant to walk on the path of goodness that God has laid down for him, and the path of goodness laid out for you by God wants to confirm the sincerity of your turning toward Him, so He brings companions who obstruct your way and try to turn you away from it.

If you obey these companions, you incline with them and go astray from the path God chose for you; but if you disobey them, you have been saved, and the schemes of the devil, who adorns for you falsehood, whether from the devils of mankind or the devils of the jinn, have failed against you.

It is as if the Shaytan (devil) only came to test the faith of the believer. He whispers to everyone and makes evil appealing to everyone, but the one of strong faith stands before this whispering and recognizes its source, so he does not obey it. As for the one of weak faith, he is led along and falls into disobedience. Had there been no Shaytan, faith would have been a monotony with nothing opposing it; but the opponent exists, and despite that the people of faith remain steadfast in their faith.

His words: "fa-zayyanu lahum ma bayna aydihim wa-ma khalfahum" (And they made fair-seeming to them what was before them and what was behind them). "What was before them": the present existing desires; "what was behind them": that is, what awaits them of the matter of the Resurrection and reckoning. "And the word has been justified against them among nations that passed away before them, of jinn and mankind; indeed they were losers."

The Arabs in ancient times were distinguished by an innate linguistic faculty (malakah 'arabiyyah), a taste for language and skill in its styles and arts. The evidence is that they made gatherings and markets for poetry. While other nations held exhibitions and markets to promote their goods, the Arabs had no merchandise except speech and eloquence, so they established a market for it in which they recited their finest poetry, then chose the best of it and hung it on the curtains of the Ka'bah, which is the noblest place on earth. This is something that did not happen in any other nation.

Therefore, Allah the Exalted chose the Arab nation to receive His method and to convey His call to His creation, and the Qur'an was revealed to them because they are the only nation that would understand and taste His language.

So: the Qur'an came to a nation that excelled in language and eloquence, so that it would be the arena of challenge. When they are unable to meet the challenge of the Qur'an, the inability of others is all the more so. Also, Allah did not grant them any advancement in anything other than their linguistic and rhetorical advancement, because the key to the religion and the miracle of the message would be the Qur'an.

Had this nation been a nation of advancement and civilization in any field other than language, they would have called Islam a civilizational revolution. No, it is not a civilized nation but an unlettered (ummiyyah) nation, and its messenger was also unlettered.

From here, unlettered-ness was a distinction and an honour for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), but it is not an honour for us, because the unlettered-ness of the Messenger of Allah means that no information from humans entered him; all his knowledge is from Allah. So who then raised him, who disciplined him, who taught him? Allah.

If the nation is unlettered and its messenger is unlettered, this is evidence that all the sources of good in this nation are not from humans.

Also, this nation is distinguished by being a nation without a homeland. The Arab's homeland is his tent, which he sets up wherever water and grass are found, and he carries it on his camel to any other place when the water dries up or the pasture ends. He has no homeland and no building that would be hard for him to leave; his house is on the back of his camel. Therefore Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And of the hides of livestock He has made for you houses which you find light [to carry] on the day you travel and the day you camp…﴾ [al-Nahl 80].

Another matter, and the most important: the Arabs were always in a state of fighting, and wars continued among the tribes for forty years. These wars made them all people of experience in the arts of war and combat. Therefore, when the Messenger of Allah needed soldiers to spread his call, he did not train anyone for fighting; rather he found soldiers ready and prepared for battle. Hence there were no military schools or training camps.

If we take into account that the Arab had no homeland to which he was bound, and that he had capability and competence in the arts of fighting, bearing in mind that it is easy to form an army and easy to send groups here and there carrying the banner of Islam, and the Messenger of Allah indeed sent them to Persia, to Byzantium, to Abyssinia, etc., this made it easy for them.

Therefore the Messenger of Allah had no standing, prepared army dedicated to fighting, because he had no need for such an army. If he wished to fight, he would simply call out "Hayya 'ala al-jihad" (come to jihad), and the Companions, especially the young among them, would gather around him, racing to go out with the Messenger of Allah, to the extent that the Messenger of Allah would select from them, saying: this one goes out and this one does not. Whoever was not chosen by the Messenger of Allah would become angry and might weep, because he had not gone out to fight with the Messenger of Allah.

So: this nation was distinguished by several qualities that qualified it to be the vessel of Allah's method and the conveyance of His message. First: it was a nation of eloquence and rhetoric. Second: it was a nation of wandering, with no settled homeland. Third: they had knowledge of the arts of war and combat and did not need training in camps; rather they were in full readiness, whenever they heard a cry (ha'ya) they flew to it. By this nature they were prepared to bear this mission.

The saying of Allah the Exalted, relating about the disbelievers of Quraysh: ﴿And those who disbelieve say, "Do not listen to this Qur'an and talk noisily during [its recitation] that you may overcome."﴾ [Fussilat 26] came as a result of the Arab's mastery of the language, his taste for it, and his understanding of its meanings. For if they let the people listen to Muhammad as he recites the Qur'an, they would inevitably be affected by it, and inevitably incline toward it and be drawn to it. So what is the solution?

Their solution: ﴿Do not listen to this Qur'an…﴾ [Fussilat 26], because they knew with certainty that if they listened, the Qur'an would captivate them with the beauty of its style, the majesty of its meanings, and the strength of its delivery. Had they known otherwise, they would not have forbidden their people from listening to it.

The matter did not stop at forbidding listening; they also created noise to disrupt it when it was recited: ﴿and make noise during it that you may overcome﴾ [Fussilat 26]. So the means of victory, in their view, was not to listen to the Qur'an and to disrupt it while it is recited, so that no opportunity is given to the listener to reflect. Their saying ﴿that you may…﴾ [Fussilat 26] means: there is a possibility you will prevail; if you do this, it is something uncertain in their view.

The evidence for this is that they believed in the eloquence and the inimitability of the Qur'an. In the end, when their stratagems were exhausted, they said of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he was mad, and Allah refuted them, saying to His Messenger: ﴿And indeed, you are of a great moral character﴾ [al-Qalam 4]. Can the mad have character, and a great character?

They said that while they knew the truthfulness of the Messenger of Allah, his trustworthiness, and his good conduct among them. They said: he is a sorcerer, and the reply to this is easy: if Muhammad had bewitched those who believed in him, why did he not bewitch you as he bewitched them, and the matter would end? And they said: he is a poet, and they lied as well, because they are a nation of speech and eloquence, and they know well what poetry is, and they had not tested anything of this kind against Muhammad.

In the end they acknowledged the truthfulness of the Qur'an, its eloquence, and its inimitability, but they objected to its being revealed to Muhammad in particular. They said: ﴿And they say, "Why was this Qur'an not sent down upon a man of importance from the two cities?"﴾ [al-Zukhruf 31].

The flaw, then, is not in the Qur'an; the Qur'an is beyond reproach. The flaw is in its being revealed to Muhammad, who was poor and one of the common people, not one of their chiefs such as 'Utbah, Shaybah, or others. Thus they acknowledged and bore witness to the Qur'an that it is a complete book encompassing all aspects of goodness and the perfections of character necessary for the welfare of this world and the Hereafter. So their objection was to the person of the Messenger of Allah, not to the Qur'an.

But they did not realise that their testimony to the Qur'an and their acknowledgment of its inimitability is more worthy in the sight of the Messenger of Allah than your testimony for it, because those who believed in Allah and in the revelation of Allah were closer to the Messenger of Allah than those who denied it.

The Romans did not believe Muhammad, but they believe in a Book, in revelation and in messengers, whereas Persia did not have the faith that the Romans had. So the hearts of the Messenger of Allah and the believers inclined toward the Romans, because they were People of the Book who believe in Allah, for the Messenger of Allah's zeal for his Lord was greater than his zeal for himself. Do you not see that the Muslims grieved when the Romans were defeated, and rejoiced when they were victorious after that?

The Almighty does not leave the punishment for sins until the Hereafter, lest the people of falsehood persist in their falsehood. Rather, Allah hastens for the people of falsehood a measure of punishment in this world before the punishment of the Hereafter, and the punishment of the Hereafter is more severe. Therefore, the Exalted addressed His Messenger (ﷺ) saying: ﴿So whether We show you some of what We promise them, or We take you [in death], to Us they will be returned﴾ [Ghafir: 77].

Then the Almighty says:

﴿That is the recompense of the enemies of…﴾.

That is, the punishment mentioned earlier. "Al-judud" (jud, denial) is intense rejection. When the disbelievers took their stance against Islam, and it became clear to them that those who called them to error and led them astray were liars, they came to hold a grudge, not against the believers, but against the disbelievers who led them astray and kept them far from faith. Therefore on the Day of Resurrection they will search for them, to take revenge on them and to place them under their feet, and a battle and a dispute will take place between the two groups, the followers and the followed:

﴿And those who disbelieved will say: "Our Lord, show us those who led us astray, both jinn and humans, that we may place them under our feet so that they will be among the lowest."﴾

Al-Sha'rawi's commentary on surah 41, verse 29:

The Real (al-Haqq), glory be to Him, depicts for us in more than one place of the Qur'an this verbal battle that takes place between the misguided and those who misguide them, and how each of the two blames the other and disclaims responsibility for himself.

Therefore Iblis will overcome those who followed him into error, and the stronger proof will be his, as Allah the Exalted said, relating his words: ﴿And I had no authority over you, except that I invited you and you responded to me. So do not blame me, but blame yourselves. I cannot help you, nor can you help me.﴾ [Ibrahim: 22].

That is: there is no authority of proof that could convince you, and no authority of force that could compel you to act. It is strange that the disbelievers, in this standing on the Day of Resurrection, say ﴿Our Lord, show us those who misled us...﴾ [Fussilat: 29]. Now they say "Our Lord" and acknowledge His lordship, may He be exalted. The meaning of ﴿that we may put them under our feet so that they will be among the lowest﴾ [Fussilat: 29] is: we will punish them ourselves before You punish them, O Lord. Their words ﴿under our feet...﴾ [Fussilat: 29] mean a punishment of humiliation, not a punishment of pain.

Then He, glory be to Him, says:

﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah"...﴾.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 41, verse 30:

They say: "Our Lord is Allah." There are two terms, rabb (Lord) and ilah (god), and each of the two has its own scope and meaning. The Rabb is the One who nurtures, creates, and cares for us, bestowing blessings and favours upon us. From it comes our saying: "nurabbihi," meaning: we give him what qualifies him for his task. So Allah is the Rabb who created from non-existence and supplied those who had been non-existent, and He continues to take us with a tenderness placed in some of us towards others, until we grow strong and our arms become firm. Then, after that, He imposes upon us the obligation of worship that belongs to divinity (ulūhiyyah).

Thus, the bounty of lordship (ʿaṭāʾ al-rubūbiyyah) is a general bounty that encompasses the believer and the disbeliever, the obedient and the disobedient. Allah is the Lord of all; His grace embraces all His creation. He created you and created for you the means of your life before He created you, and He made for you an intellect by which you distinguish and choose between alternatives. If you use your intellect well in what He has given you of means, you will reap its fruit; if you do not use it well, you are the loser. So the bounty of lordship is for all, and the means are available to all, giving whoever deserves to be given, even if he is a disbeliever...

For this reason we often wonder at Allah's wide giving to non-believers, and that in their hands are all the delights and adornments of this world, while the believer is deprived of them. There is no wonder in that, because this is the bounty of lordship, and these people used the means well, so the means gave to them. If you too used them well, the means would give to you...

So His saying: "Indeed, those who said, 'Our Lord is Allah'..." means: they acknowledged Him, glory be to Him, as Lord, and affirmed that He is the One who created us, nurtured us, gave to us and bestowed favours upon us. And it is remarkable that He did not impose obligations upon us until we reached our maturity (ashudd). That is, He left me to grow in this world and bestowed His blessings for fifteen years without imposing anything upon me. Why?

Because He does not impose obligation upon you except after the completion of your formation and the perfection of your strength... So obligation only comes after the age of puberty and the completion of manhood. And the One who imposes obligation upon us is Allah. The Rabb created, provided and nurtured, and Allah imposed obligation and commanded worship. Allah is the One worshipped, meaning: obeyed in His command and prohibition. Before He is obeyed in His command and prohibition, He gave you the gift of lordship. It is as if He advanced the good to you before commanding you to worship Him, so the least you can do is to advance good by obeying the One who nurtured you...

So we say: lordship is a gift, and divinity is an obligation, but it is an obligation that first gives to you, because you are in this world, and the age of this world is the measure of your own existence in it. You have no part in the age of the world from Adam until the Hour, for all that time does not concern you, and it is decreed by Allah in length: this one lives ten years, this one fifty, this one a hundred. So the length of one's term is not in anyone's hands.

After the Truthful One (al-Haqq, subhanahu) mentioned to us a portion of the rebellious nations who opposed the messengers and what their affair came to of punishment, He mentions the counterpart, who are the people of faith and steadfastness upon the path, and says, exalted is He: "Indeed, those who said, 'Our Lord is Allah,' and then remained steadfast..." We said: action is speech and deed. Speech is the action of the tongue, and its counterpart is deed, which is the action of the rest of the limbs: sight is for the eye, hearing for the ear, touch for the hands, striving for the feet, and so on. And each of speech and deed is called an action.

What, then, is the action of the heart? The heart, materially, is the organ responsible for pumping the blood, the liquid of life, to the rest of the body's parts, and it is the vessel of faith and belief. When it is filled with certainty and faith, it disseminates that into every particle of the body. Therefore we say: the action of the heart is belief (iʿtiqād), and ʿaqīdah (creed) is the knotted thing that is not undone, the thing that has settled in the heart so that it does not come out again for the intellect to debate.

We say: an idea is first presented to the intellect to examine and discuss it, and if it is satisfied with it, it delivers it to the heart so that a firm creed settles in it. The heart, then, only receives firm creeds, and these creeds are what will be the principle for you in the movements of your life.

From here we know the importance and gravity of the role of the tongue. It has half the work, and the rest of the limbs have the other half. It is the one that expresses you and reveals what is within you. All the limbs must interact positively with the cosmos: the ear hears, the eye sees, the nose smells, the hand touches. The limbs provide me with the material of thought, and by them the believer reaches the signs of Allah in the cosmos; by them the beneficial is recognised and the harmful is recognised, so he takes the beneficial and keeps away from the harmful. The ear hears everything, and you must direct it to hear good and turn it away from hearing evil: "and when they pass by idle talk, they pass by with dignity" (Qur'an 25:72).

And the eye looks by which you see the marvellous making of Allah in His cosmos, and lowers its gaze from what He has forbidden. Here is the cosmos before you, an open book, and all you have to do is read what is in it of signs and miracles. The heavens and what is in them of sun, moon, stars, celestial bodies and galaxies all move with a precise, firm order, and the earth and what is in it of elements and what it grows for us of good things...

When a person is imbued with the creed of faith, he declares it with his tongue, joyfully. Here comes the role of the tongue, which expresses what is in the heart and leads the rest of the limbs. Therefore it is related in the noble hadith that our master, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), said: "There is not a day but the limbs call out to the tongue, saying: 'Fear Allah concerning us, for we are only through you. If you are upright, we are upright, and if you are crooked, we are crooked.'"

So His saying, exalted is He, "Indeed, those who said, 'Our Lord is Allah'," indicates the saying of the believers, which faith has taken root in their hearts, and which the tongues express: "Our Lord is Allah," our Creator and Nurturer, who created us from non-existence, supplied us from non-existence, and gave us security and safety, for He is the One who said: "Neither drowsiness nor sleep overtakes Him" (Qur'an 2:255).

If a person wants a guard, he hires a guard for himself, so how is it when his guard sleeps? But you, O believer, are under Allah's protection, so sleep with a heart at peace, for your guard is not overtaken by drowsiness or sleep.

So the believer, when he experiences all this bounty, and when he sees the means of his life within his reach, food and drink, security and peace, air he breathes and earth that gives him all he desires, rejoices in Allah's gift to him and cannot but say "Our Lord is Allah," because it has become a firm creed in the heart.

And since your Lord is Allah, do not grieve or worry about the affairs of this world, for Allah is the One who takes charge of your affair. You see the child in his father's life bearing no care of anything, and not thinking about the rise of prices, or the provision of food, goods and clothing, etc., because his father is present. How much more so if Allah is the One who takes charge of you? By Allah, the true believer is ashamed to bear the concern of sustenance or livelihood, while he knows that his Lord is Allah.

And since "our Lord is Allah," there is no distress, and you are a servant (rabb, here "lord" in the sense of owner/master, as is said of the master of a house). Your Lord will take charge of you, and will keep every evil away from you, and will suffice you for everything that concerns you.

You remember the story of Moses, peace be upon him, with Pharaoh. When Pharaoh pursued him with his armies...

"The companions of Moses said: 'Indeed, we are to be overtaken!'" (Qur'an 26:61). This is how the reality of events speaks: before them is the sea, and behind them are Pharaoh's soldiers, and there is no escape. But what did Moses say? He said: "No!" (kallā), meaning: they will not overtake us, and will not reach us. He said it from his store of faith and his trust in his Lord and His protection of him, for Allah would not send a messenger and then hand him over to his enemy.

"He said: 'No! Indeed, with me is my Lord; He will guide me'" (Qur'an 26:62). So relief came to him from his Lord at once: "Then We revealed to Moses: 'Strike the sea with your staff,' and it parted, and each part was like a huge mountain" (Qur'an 26:63).

Reflect here on Allah's guarding of His friends, and reflect on this miracle and this lordship. As soon as Moses uttered his word with sincere faith, the response came. Allah removed from the water the property of fluidity, and the water froze, so he walked on both sides, each part like a mighty mountain, and in the middle there was a dry, parched path, which Moses and his soldiers crossed.

When he reached the other shore, he wanted to strike the sea again, to return it to its fluidity and close the path in the face of Pharaoh. But his Lord guided him and corrected his point of view, for Allah has another plan, and the situation was not yet over. So Allah said to Moses: "Leave the sea at rest; indeed, they are an army to be drowned" (Qur'an 44:24).

After Allah had saved Moses and his people and led them to the desert, He gave the same staff another role: "And when Moses asked for water for his people, We said: 'Strike the rock with your staff,' and there gushed forth from it twelve springs..." (Qur'an 2:60). So the staff is one, and he strikes with it the water so that it becomes a mountain, and strikes with it the mountain so that it gushes with water. The effect differs, because the Doer is Allah, the Able.

His saying, exalted is He, "Our Lord is Allah," gives us a general idea of the gift of lordship in respect of material and of values. Your Lord, who supplied you with the means of matter, would not leave you without the means of spirit and values. Just as you have taken His blessings in food, drink and dwelling, take His blessings in obligation, for by obligation He nurtures spirit and values in you.

Here we should reflect, for example, on His saying: "O Children of Adam! We have sent down to you clothing to cover your private parts and as an adornment; but the clothing of righteousness, that is best. That is among the signs of Allah, that they may remember" (Qur'an 7:26).

So Allah gave you the necessary clothing, which is what covers your nakedness, then He added to you the ar-riyash, which is the luxury of clothing and the adornment by which a person shows off.

But do not forget that the clothing of righteousness, that is better, meaning: better than the first clothing. The clothing of matter covers your nakedness in this world, but the clothing of righteousness covers you in this world and saves you in the Hereafter.

So it is a gift that extends, remains, and is eternal in the Hereafter. It is therefore the best clothing for whoever is mindful and understands. So your Lord, by His lordship over us, gave us what sustains our matter and what makes our worldly life happy, and He, glory be to Him, would not leave our hearts empty of the moral and spiritual values that make us happy in the Hereafter...

And reflect on this affirmation by the believers when they said "Our Lord is Allah": an affirmation that combines the gift of lordship, acknowledgement of it, and the gift of divinity. The Lord is the same as the God; the Giver is the same, glory be to Him, as the One who imposes obligation. Whoever has accepted from his Lord the gift of lordship and received His blessings, bringing into existence from non-existence and supplying from non-existence, it is not fitting for him to abandon His obligations, especially since they are obligations that make a person happy in this world and the Hereafter, which did not come to constrain him or to burden him.

The gift of lordship is also present in the gift of divinity. It is known that the obligations came as "do" and "do not": you must do what is commanded, and stop at what is forbidden. And what has no text is left to you: you are free in it, to do or not to do.

Then, exalted is He, says, relating about the believers, after they said "Our Lord is Allah" and acknowledged to Allah, exalted is He, lordship and divinity, and this belief settled in them firm and steadfast: "then they remained steadfast" (thumma istaqāmū), meaning: after the saying came the action.

Reflect here on the conjunction thumma, for in the language it indicates sequence and delay. Glory be to Him did not say "fa-istaqāmū" (so they stood firm), for a wisdom: it is as if the Truthful One wanted to give you an opportunity to reflect on this creed, to examine it and be convinced of it. He gave you an opportunity to review this creed within yourself, so that you believe in it by consent and act by it by conviction, so that you embrace it in a love that may reach you to the degree of passion for this steadfastness.

The meaning of istiqāmah is: taking a thing upon its straightness (qawām). It requires walking on a straight line, which Allah has named the straight path (al-ṣirāṭ al-mustaqīm). So Allah wants from you, O believer, that you make the means to the end of the work of obligation like the path: you do not incline from it the breadth of a hair, nor deviate from its course.

For when you walk along a wide street, you may in walking go here once and there once. Yes, that is permitted to you, but do not forget that it lengthens the distance for you and increases the hardship.

Therefore Allah named His path that leads to His Garden "the straight path" (al-ṣirāṭ al-mustaqīm) (Qur'an 1:6), and in another place He said "the even way" (sawāʾ al-sabīl) (Qur'an 2:108), meaning: in its middle, without deviation.

If the goal is distant, it requires of you, to reach it, hastening in movement so that you attain what you want. How much more so for one whose goal is the Garden? Without doubt he hastens towards it and spares no effort in reaching it.

Therefore we say: the believer should not hate death, for it will bring him to his goal; he only hates it if his deed is not righteous. Yes, he hates to meet Allah while he is not in righteousness. When the result appears, for example, you see the diligent student hastening to it: why? Because he is confident of it. But the lazy one you see slow and unconcerned.

Therefore our Lord, blessed and exalted, teaches us: "And hasten to forgiveness from your Lord and a Garden whose breadth is the heavens and the earth, prepared for the God-fearing" (Qur'an 3:133).

And He said, describing the believers: "Indeed, they used to hasten to good works" (Qur'an 21:90). The meaning: beware lest your worldly life preoccupy you, or restrict your movement towards the Hereafter; rather, hasten and speed in its direction, for you do not know how much of the road you will cover before death overtakes you.

And of His justice, glory be to Him, toward His servant: He took for Himself the servant's lifespan in length, but left him two other dimensions, breadth and depth. How? They said: your life in terms of time is length, which none knows but Allah, and none holds its end but Allah alone. But He left to you the choice to extend in breadth as you wish. You can invest the moment you are living in and expand the circle of good within it. Thus breadth is greater than length, and the measure is not the length of life but the amount of righteous action within it.

Some people do in a short life noble deeds that the one with a long life does not do. Therefore, when Allah described the Garden to us, He said: "And hasten to forgiveness from your Lord and a Garden whose breadth is the heavens and the earth, prepared for the God-fearing" (Qur'an 3:133).

He mentioned the breadth, and if its breadth is the heavens and the earth, what of its length?

Then He gave you another dimension, which is depth. Depth in one's life belongs to a person after his death and the cessation of his works in this world, by his good effect remaining and extending through the depth of time.

And the Truthful One, when He commands us to walk the straight path, and when He commands us to hasten to good works, wants for us only the easiest ways that lead us to the noblest goals with the least effort. And it is known to the scholars of geometry that the straight line is the shortest way and the least distance between two points...

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 41, verse 31:

Meaning: your helpers, those close to you, and those who support you in this world and in the Hereafter. They said: the angels were created disposed to obedience; therefore, when Adam was created, they said: ﴿Will You place therein one who will cause corruption therein and shed blood, while we exalt You with praise and sanctify You?﴾ [al-Baqarah: 30] Allah replied to them: ﴿Indeed, I know that which you do not know﴾ [al-Baqarah: 30].

Meaning: I created the angels disposed to obedience, ﴿who do not disobey Allah in what He commands them, and they do what they are commanded﴾ [al-Tahrim: 6]. But what I want is one who obeys without being able to disobey; rather, I want another creation that does not come to Me by compulsion. They come to Me willingly, and they draw near to Me out of love, while they are able to disobey. They come to Me by choice, not by subjugation or coercion.

We had already given an example for this, and we said: suppose you have two servants. You tie one of them and bind him to you with a chain, and the other is free and unrestrained. You call out to them, and they both hasten to you. Which of them will be more obedient to you than the other?

So His saying ﴿We are your allies﴾ [Fussilat: 31] means: We come to you in hardship and support you, and in trial We give you patience.

Therefore, it is reported in the noble hadith that one of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sat reciting the Qur'an, and beside him was a horse. He heard from it a cry and a murmur, and he saw from it a strange movement, and he saw above his head a light. He went to our master the Messenger of Allah and told him of that. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "This is from the angels' allegiance to us in this world." In the Hereafter, they are allies too, because they will be deputies of Allah in resurrection, in reckoning, and in welcoming the people of Paradise with greeting, as the True One, glory be to Him, related: ﴿Peace be upon you, you have been good, so enter it, abiding therein﴾ [al-Zumar: 73].

And He said: ﴿Peace be upon you for what you patiently endured; how excellent is the final home﴾ [al-Ra'd: 24]. This is the greeting of the angels. Then Allah Himself greets them likewise, as in Surah Yasin: ﴿Peace, a word from a Lord, Most Merciful﴾ [Ya-Sin: 58].

﴿And for you therein is whatever your souls desire, and for you therein is whatever you ask for﴾ [Fussilat: 31]. They said: whatever the soul seeks of delight, you find before you as soon as it occurs to your mind. So what luxury is this? We have gone to many countries and entered the greatest hotels there, and the utmost they reached is that you press a certain button that gives you coffee, for example, and another button that gives you tea. Is there anything greater than what Allah has prepared for you in Paradise? The moment a thing occurs to your mind, you find it before you. Moreover, therein is of delight "what no eye has seen, nor ear has heard, nor has it occurred to the heart of any human."

Therefore, when He, glory be to Him, wished to depict Paradise for us, He did not describe it explicitly; rather He said, glory be to Him: ﴿The likeness of Paradise which the righteous have been promised﴾ [Muhammad: 15], its likeness, not itself. Why? They said: because the words of language are set for meanings and referents, and the meaning must first exist, and then we assign to it the word that signifies it. The non-existent has no word that denotes it. (The television), for example, before they invented it, what was its name? It had no name; it was non-existent.

Likewise, there are no words in language now that denote the delights of Paradise, because we do not know them nor know the names of these things. They are things which no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and which have not occurred to the heart of any human. So from where would the words denoting them come?

His saying ﴿And for you therein﴾ [Fussilat: 31], i.e., in Paradise, ﴿is whatever your souls desire﴾ [Fussilat: 31]: what is meant is the souls of faith that stood firm upon the path of Allah. There is nothing forbidden in Paradise, and no one in Paradise desires forbidden things. The soul desires the lawful. Even the forbidden things of this world, if they exist in the Hereafter, are another thing, from which the cause of prohibition has been removed.

Thus wine in this world is known to take away the intellect, and that there is no pleasure in drinking it. As for the wine of the Hereafter, Allah says of it: ﴿and rivers of wine, delicious to the drinkers﴾ [Muhammad: 15].

And you see in films, for example, how the one who drinks wine drinks it: he pours it into his mouth like this, all at once, why? Because its taste is disgusting, and he wants to pass it quickly through the region of taste. But the one who drinks a cup of mango juice, for example, you see him sipping it sip by sip, which we call "yumzumz" it, because its taste is delightful and its aroma is delightful.

Likewise, in all the delights of Paradise that have a counterpart in this world, you find the True One, glory be to Him, purifying it from impurities and freeing it from the harms we know in this world. Reflect on His saying, exalted be He, about the water of the Hereafter: ﴿rivers of water unchanging﴾ [Muhammad: 15], meaning it does not change and does not suffer staleness like the water of this world. And regarding milk He said: ﴿and rivers of milk whose taste does not change﴾ [Muhammad: 15], and He said regarding honey: ﴿and rivers of purified honey﴾ [Muhammad: 15].

So: do not say, "wine like the wine of this world," nor "water like the water of this world," nor "milk like the milk you drink." No, these are delights of another kind, which the Creator, glory be to Him, has purified and cleansed of its impurities.

﴿And for you therein is whatever you ask for﴾ [Fussilat: 31], i.e., for you in Paradise is everything you wish for and everything you seek.

The Nuzul (lodging, provision) is the place prepared for a guest in which he stays, and this place must be prepared so that the guest finds in it everything he wants. It is the home of generosity; for this reason we call the hotel a nuzul. Yes, a nuzul prepared by humans for humans. But Paradise is a nuzul prepared by the Lord of humankind and their Creator, prepared for them by the Forgiving, the Merciful toward them.

Therefore we said: when we went to (San Francisco) we found there hotels of a high degree of refinement and quality of service, and I saw admiration for them in the eyes of my colleagues. So I wanted to draw their attention to a faith-based observation, and I said to them: You marvel at what you see; look at it with a contemplative gaze. This is what humans have prepared for humans, so how about what Allah, the Lord of humankind, has prepared for humankind?...

And His saying: ﴿A provision from the Forgiving, the Merciful﴾ indicates that this provision and this bliss are not attained by the servant through his deeds, but are attained through the forgiveness and mercy of Allah. This explains to us the noble Prophetic hadith: "None of you will enter Paradise by his deeds." They said: "Not even you, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Not even I, unless Allah covers me with His mercy."

Following the completion of His discussion of the innate perfection of the believer who has perfected his faith and declared, "My Lord is Allah," and then remained steadfast upon this path, the Truth, glory be to Him, says (after the believer has received faith and its sweetness has touched his heart) that this faith overflows from him to others. This is one of the duties of the believer: to convey faith and to convey goodness to others.

The believer loves for his brother what he loves for himself, and is keen to reform the society around him. The believer does not stop at his own self, and is never selfish.
