Even the People of the Book, Jews and Christians, who took the religion of God as a religion without worldly authority, the Qur'an dealt with them justly, saying of them: ﴿And among the People of the Book is one who, if you entrust him with a heap of gold, will return it to you; and among them is one who, if you entrust him with a single dinar, will not return it to you unless you keep standing over him.﴾ [Al 'Imran: 75]

After that, the Qur'an comes and passes judgment on people that they will never believe and never be guided, while they are in the breadth of worldly life and in a time of choice: whoever wills, let him believe, and whoever wills, let him disbelieve. Yet they remained in their disbelief and did not believe, not even hypocritically. And had it been out of desire to deny the Qur'an, it would not have happened...

So God, exalted, is the possessor of forgiveness for every disbeliever, every denier, and every opponent who returns to the right path, repents and turns back in penitence, and the possessor of painful punishment for whoever persists in his disbelief, continues in his opposition, and clashes with the call to truth.

It is not hidden that combining a meaning and its opposite in one place is one of the features of the Qur'anic style, because the opposite is made manifest by its opposite, and things are distinguished by their contraries. Your Lord informs you and leaves it to you to choose for yourself the motives of forgiveness or the motives of punishment.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 41, verse 44:

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿And had We made it⦅the Qur'an⦆ a non-Arabic recitation⦾﴾. The Qur'an is so named because it is recited (qur'an). ﴿Non-Arabic⦾﴾ means in the language of the non-Arabs (a'jam), those who are not Arabs, such as English, French and other languages other than Arabic.

﴿They would have said: "Why are its verses not made clear?"⦾﴾ That is, it would have come in Arabic...

So the Truthful, glorified is He, explains that if the Qur'an had been revealed in a non-Arabic language, they would have sought and wished that it were in Arabic. Yet, regardless of the language in which it was revealed, it is in its essence guidance and healing. ﴿Say: "It is, for those who believe, guidance and healing. And as for those who do not believe, there is deafness in their ears, and it is blindness for them."⦾﴾ That is, those who do not believe in it have deafness in their ears, so they do not hear the beneficial, fruitful hearing. ﴿And it is blindness for them⦾﴾ means darkness and doubts in which they stumble.

So the Qur'an is one, but the outcome differs, because the reception of the Qur'an differs according to the intention of the one who receives it. The one who hears it with an attentive ear and a pure heart, not preoccupied with its opposite, finds it guidance and finds it healing. The one who hears it with arrogance and a heart not prepared for faith finds it blindness, and the blind man stumbles, not knowing where to head.

Thus, one who recites the Qur'an or hears it without understanding it or being affected by it: concerning such people Allah said: ﴿And among them are those who listen to you, until, when they go out from your presence, they say to those who were given knowledge, "What did he just say?"⦾﴾ [Muhammad: 16].

We have already explained the theory of the agent and the receptive (al-fa'il wa al-qabil). The agent performs the action and the receptive is affected by it. There is a difference between the farmer who strikes the earth with his hoe and one who strikes a rock with it, for example. The earth responds to the hoe, is affected by it, and bears fruit and produces, whereas the rock does not accept and is not affected.

So you should not judge a thing unless this interaction between agent and receptive has taken place. You remember that we gave the example in this matter of a hot cup of tea that you blow on to cool it, and you blow on your hands to warm them: the breath is one, but the effect differs according to the receptive.

As for His words, may He be exalted: ﴿Those are called from a far place⦾﴾, because they heard but were not affected by it, Allah likened them to one who is called from afar and does not hear.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 41, verse 45:

The Qur'an here relates to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) a portion of the story of our master Musa (peace be upon him). This is among ﴿Nothing is said to you except what was said to the messengers before you﴾ [Fussilat: 43], and Musa is among the messengers who bore hardship and obstinacy, and whose people wearied him. So his story here is a consolation for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). ﴿And We certainly gave Musa the Book﴾ [Fussilat: 45], i.e., the Torah, ﴿but differences arose concerning it﴾ [Fussilat: 45], i.e., it became a field for their disagreement. Some of them distorted it, some of them forgot part of it, and some of them wrote the book with their own hands and said: "This is from Allah."

﴿And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord﴾ [Fussilat: 45], i.e., a word and wisdom of Allah had preceded that the punishment of total annihilation, which seizes the deniers entirely, would be deferred, as we saw with 'Ad, Thamud, the people of Nuh and the people of Lut. As for this Ummah, Allah will not seize it with the like of this in the world; rather He defers its recompense until the Day of Resurrection.

﴿And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord, it would have been judged between them﴾ [Fussilat: 45], i.e., in this world, as He did with the earlier nations who denied the messengers. ﴿And indeed they (your people, O Muhammad) are in disquieting doubt concerning it﴾ [Fussilat: 45], meaning: a hesitation that leads them to anxiety and suspicion.

Doubt (shakk) is one of the six well-known relations (nisab) that affect occurrences. The first is knowledge ('ilm), which is that you have a proposition that corresponds to reality, you are convinced of it, and you are able to present the proof for it.

Then imitation (taqlid), which is that you have a proposition that corresponds to reality, you are convinced of it, but you are unable to present proof for it. For example, we teach a small child that Allah is One, and he believes it out of trust in his father who teaches him, because he knows that his father wishes him well and teaches him only what is right; yet the father himself cannot establish proof that Allah is One.

Then ignorance (jahl), which is that you have a proposition that does not correspond to reality, and you are convinced of it. Therefore we have said on this matter: the ignorant person is harder on his teacher than the unlettered (ummi), because the ignorant person holds a false, untrue proposition and believes in it, so he requires from you double effort: once to bring him out of his ignorance, and once to convince him of the truth. As for the unlettered, his mind is blank; he has no proposition to defend, so you find him compliant, accepting what is presented to him without disputing.

Then after that doubt (shakk), which is that you have a proposition that corresponds to reality, but your certainty about it is equal to your doubt about it, so you are not sure of it. Then, if affirmation and confirmation are more evident, it is opinion (zann); and if doubt is more evident than certainty, it is delusion (wahm).

So the words of the Exalted: ﴿And indeed they are in disquieting doubt concerning it﴾ [Fussilat: 45] mean: they have not reached the level of knowledge, nor the level of imitation, nor the level of ignorance.

Al-Sha'rawi's commentary on surah 41, verse 46:

The Almighty here establishes a factual reality which He wants His servants to believe in, so that it becomes firmly fixed in their minds that each one of them works for the benefit of himself, and that the faith of believers returns nothing to God Most High, and does not add to Him any attribute He did not already have.

Likewise, the disobedience of the disobedient does not harm Him, nor does the denial of the deniers or the rejection of those who reject, because He, glory be to Him, possesses all attributes of majesty, beauty and perfection before He created this creation. God Most High has no need whatsoever for the obedience of the obedient or the faith of believers; rather, the servants are the ones who benefit from their righteous deeds.

The commands of the sacred law are nothing but God Most High's concern for His creation and the mercy of the Maker toward His handiwork, for every maker wants good for his creation and guards it against corruption and the causes of ruin.

You know the hadith qudsi: "O My servants, you are free: whoever believes, believes, and whoever disbelieves, disbelieves, and each is recompensed for his deeds." ﴿Whoever does righteousness, it is for his own soul﴾ [Fussilat: 46], he is the one who benefits, and I have no share in his deed. ﴿And whoever does evil, it is against it﴾ [Fussilat: 46], i.e., his evil is recorded against his own self. This is a matter that your Lord, mighty and majestic, has decreed, and it is up to you to choose for yourself, and to lead it to the course that makes it happy, not the one that makes it wretched.

It is strange that a human being, after knowing this truth, leads himself into the paths of destruction; therefore the Almighty described him as "a wrongdoer and ignorant" (ظلوم وجهول).

When the Almighty warns us of punishment, and when He makes it severe, it is not in His interest to inflict this punishment upon the servants; rather He wants to turn us away from its causes and frighten us of them so that we do not fall into them. God Most High is exalted above injustice: ﴿And your Lord is not ever unjust to the servants﴾ [Fussilat: 46].

He frightens you for your own protection. Consider when He says to us: "Whoever kills shall be killed" (مَنْ قتل يُقتل). Does He want people to be killed, or does He want to preserve blood and protect it? And who would commit murder while knowing that whoever kills will be killed?

Therefore, regarding military strength, you find the Qur'an saying: ﴿And prepare against them whatever you are able of power and of steeds of war, by which you may terrify the enemy of Allah and your enemy...﴾ [al-Anfal: 60].

It is strange that the enemies of Islam take from this verse proof that Islam supports terrorism, because it mentions the word (turhibun, "you terrify"). This is a mistaken understanding of the style of the Qur'an, for the meaning of preparing a force that terrifies is that I do not want battle and I do not want confrontation; when my enemy knows that I am ready, he fears and does not proceed to fight.

You hear them in military matters saying: "balance of power." This balance is what preserves peace in the entire international community. When there were two equal powers in the world, Russia and America, there was military stability, for each of them feared the other, to the point that they called the wars between them (the Cold War). But when the power of Russia disintegrated, America came to have dominance; it is now the only power, and we see it doing what it wants without a deterrent from another power.

So we say: when the Almighty and Exalted commands us to prepare military strength, He does not mean that He is pushing us onto the battlefield; rather He means preserving peace between us and others. It is well known that you never proceed to attack one who is stronger than you, so the verse seeks peace; it does not seek terrorism as they claim.

As for His saying, glory be to Him: ﴿And your Lord is not ever unjust to the servants﴾ [Fussilat: 46], the word (ظَلاَّم, zallam) is on the pattern fa''al, and it is an intensive form (sigha mubalagha) of "zalim" (wrongdoer), like "qatil" and "qattal" (killer). When the verse negates the intensive form, that does not necessitate negating the root, which is "zalim"; the lesser attribute remains present, because if you say in affirmation "so-and-so is 'allama," this indicates that he is a knower by a fortiori; but in negation, if you say "so-and-so is not 'allama," this does not prevent him from being a knower.

So: does negating the intensive form zallam imply affirming zalim, exalted is God above injustice? They said: No, because the wording of the verse is ﴿And your Lord is not ever unjust to the servants﴾ [Fussilat: 46], and it did not say "to the servant," so the intensive form comes from the repetition of the act. That is: if He wronged a single servant, He would be a wrongdoer; but if He wronged all, then He must have great power that transforms Him into a zallam.

Thus negating zallam in this sense is also a negation of zalim, and then whoever wants to wrong, wrongs according to his power; so, supposing that the Almighty were to wrong, He would be zallam: ﴿And your Lord is not ever unjust to the servants﴾ [Fussilat: 46].

When the Almighty negates the attribute of injustice from Himself after His saying ﴿Whoever does righteousness, it is for his own soul, and whoever does evil, it is against it﴾ [Fussilat: 46], it is as if He, glory be to Him, is saying: "I am a just judge between you and your own souls. I recompense every soul according to what it has done and what it has striven for, without injustice. I judge in your favour and against you; you are not adversaries to Me."

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 41, verse 47:

The words of Allah, Exalted is He, "to Him" (ilayhi), meaning to Allah, glorified and exalted is He: ﴿To Him is referred the knowledge of the Hour.﴾ [Fussilat: 47] The Hour is the Resurrection, and its knowledge means its time. This is one of the matters Allah, Exalted is He, has kept exclusively for His knowledge, and He has not informed any of His creatures of it: ﴿None but Him will reveal it at its time. It has become heavy upon the heavens and the earth. It will not come to you except suddenly.﴾ [al-A'raf: 187] ﴿They ask you as if you were well-informed about it. Say, "Its knowledge is only with Allah, but most of the people do not know."﴾ [al-A'raf: 187]

In concealing the time of the Hour there are great wisdoms, the most important of which is that people should not become complacent, and that the people of falsehood and the people of whims and desires should not persist in their desires unchecked. Rather, everyone should prepare for it, and everyone should hasten to righteous deeds, because no one can guarantee the appointed time of his death and his departure from the world of action to the abode of reckoning. We have said before: whoever dies, his resurrection has come.

For this reason we have said that the acts of worship with set times have a period from such-and-such to such-and-such. The noon prayer, for example, is from the sun's zenith to the shadow of twice the object's length. Whoever prays during all of this period has fulfilled the obligation, but it is preferable to hasten. Why? Because you cannot guarantee your life until the end of the time. Death may reach you a moment after the time begins, and then you will have sinned.

For this reason, when the Master of the Messengers, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), was asked about the best deeds, he said: "Prayer at its appointed time." Allah, Exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, prayer has been decreed upon the believers a decree of specified times.﴾ [an-Nisa': 103] Likewise in the matter of Hajj, you see a man who is wealthy and able to bear the expenses of Hajj, yet he does not perform it. If you ask him, he says: "If I live to such-and-such a year and after such-and-such, I will perform Hajj." Glory be to Allah! Have you guaranteed that you will live until that time?

Allah, the Truth, in His wisdom, left the time of the Hour unspecified, and left the time of death unspecified, and He, glorified is He, has kept its knowledge to Himself. The Resurrection is true, and death is true, and it is an arrow already sent toward you, and your life is measured by the length of its journey and its arrival at you.

They said: The concealment of the knowledge of the Hour and of the term is itself clarity. Its being made general throughout the whole time makes you ready for it, anticipating and awaiting it at every moment. For this reason Allah, Exalted is He, said in Surat Tabarak: ﴿Blessed is He in whose hand is dominion, and He is over all things competent. [He] who created death and life to test you as to which of you is best in deed.﴾ [al-Mulk: 1-2]

He mentioned death before life in the creation, although life exists first. He mentioned death to keep it constantly in mind and in the heart. He mentioned death so that you would receive life cautiously and not be deceived by it, receiving life together with its opposite, death, so that you await it at any moment.

Among the mercies of Allah toward His servants is that He made for the Resurrection signs by which its nearness may be inferred: minor signs and major signs, in order to frighten people and awaken them from their heedlessness of the Hereafter.

His words: ﴿And no fruit comes out of its coverings﴾ [Fussilat: 47]. The "akmam" (coverings) is the plural of "kimm," which is the green sheath that encloses the fruit; then it splits little by little so that the fruit comes out of it. Just as you see, for example, the rose before it opens: you find it within a closed green sheath surrounding it, as if it were closing its eyes; then it opens and emerges from this sheath.

﴿And no female conceives or gives birth except with His knowledge﴾ [Fussilat: 47]. All of these are among the matters hidden from human knowledge, but they are not hidden from the knowledge of Allah. The phrase ﴿And no female conceives﴾ [Fussilat: 47]: pregnancy (al-hamal) is well known; it is the union of the female ovum with the male sperm, and from this union pregnancy occurs, and it is a gift from Allah in any case.

Allah, the Truth, Exalted is He, said: ﴿He bestows female [children] upon whom He wills and bestows male [children] upon whom He wills.﴾ [ash-Shura: 49]

Thus, barrenness itself is a gift for whoever reflects and seeks wisdom. When you look at the son who killed his father or his mother, and the son who brought shame upon his family so that they wished death would relieve them of him, when you look at the disobedience of children, you know that barrenness is a blessing and a gift from Allah that calls for gratitude just as the blessing of a child does.

Then you find that the Qur'anic context puts the female first, because she was disliked among the Arabs in earlier times and was not desired. For this reason Allah placed a special rank for whoever raises daughters and treats them well, and for whoever respects the decree of Allah in bearing daughters. It is as if a voice from Allah were calling to him: "My servant, as long as you have accepted My gift and My blessing, by My might and My majesty, I will surely give you for every daughter of them a husband who fulfills your hopes concerning her and who will be more dutiful to you than your sons."

In this matter of childbearing we have seen wonders that confirm the power of Allah, Exalted is He, and the freedom of this power. We have seen a couple who were not granted children and so they separated; then the man married another and had children from her, and the woman married another and had children from him. It was as if childbearing had been impossible between these two specifically.

Then when you reflect on the rational division of the matter of creation, you find that the power of Allah, Exalted is He, encompasses it in its four forms. Natural childbearing comes from a male and a female, but the power of Allah brought Adam without a husband or wife, brought Hawwa' from a father without a mother, brought Jesus from a mother without a father, and a father and mother may both exist and yet no childbearing occurs. All of these are forms that confirm the absolute freedom of divine power in the matter of creation.

The words of Allah, Exalted is He: ﴿And [mention] the day He calls them, "Where are My partners?"﴾ [Fussilat: 47] It is He, glorified is He, who says "My partners," meaning: according to your supposition, because He said in another place: ﴿Those you used to claim﴾ [al-An'am: 22]. They answered, and the speech here relates a scene from the scenes of the Resurrection: ﴿They will say, "We have informed You"﴾ [Fussilat: 47], meaning: we have told You and made You know. The "udhn" (ear) is the means of hearing, through which speech reaches and knowledge is obtained, so the ear is, as it were, the first means of knowledge.

For this reason Allah, Exalted is He, said about the earth: ﴿And it listened to its Lord and was obligated﴾ [al-Inshiqaq: 2], meaning: it gave ear to the commands. ﴿They will say, "We have informed You"﴾ [Fussilat: 47], meaning: we have told You; ﴿none of us is a witness﴾ [Fussilat: 47], meaning no one among us testifies that You have partners. Allah, Exalted is He, said ﴿My partners﴾ and did not deny the partners in order to deny them Himself.

Thus, after it is too late, they acknowledge that Allah, Exalted is He, has no partner, as if this word "partner" had never once passed over the tongue of any of them.

The meaning of ﴿And what they used to invoke before has strayed from them﴾ is: it vanished and departed from them, so it is no longer present with them, ﴿from among those they used to call upon before﴾ [Fussilat: 48], namely their protectors whom they associated with God. ﴿And they will be certain﴾ here means they became certain and sure, ﴿that there is for them no place of escape﴾ [Fussilat: 48], meaning no refuge and no way of flight that would save them from the punishment. So he looks here and there, and finds no place of refuge and no way of deliverance; the calamity is overwhelming, with no escape from it. Therefore, even in our colloquial speech we say: "Fulan ḥāyis" (so-and-so is bewildered), meaning: perplexed, finding no place to flee to.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 41, verse 49:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Man does not tire of asking for good﴾ — "does not tire" means does not grow weary. ﴿The human being﴾ — the intended meaning is the disbeliever. ﴿Of asking for good﴾ — of seeking good for himself: good in his wealth, in his children, in his health and well-being. You see a man saying: "O Lord, an apartment to live in." When God gives him the apartment, he says: "O Lord, a small villa." When God gives him that, he says: "O Lord, a building whose income covers the villa."

So the human being has been created with a love of good and with greed (and nothing fills the eye of the son of Adam except dust, and God turns in forgiveness to whoever repents), and few of the people are those who take matters in their proper measure.

Our master Dawud (peace be upon him and upon our Prophet) was given by God much of good things, yet one day he sat on the roof of his house and saw a swarm of golden locusts. He spread out his garment and began gathering the locusts into it. God manifested Himself to him and said: "O Dawud, did I not make you rich?" He said: "Yes, O Lord, but I have no independence from Your bounty."

If this was the condition of the Prophet of God Dawud, then what of the ordinary believer? And what of those who are not believers, like those concerning whom this verse was revealed, and of whom God said: ﴿And I do not think the Hour will be established; and even if I am returned to my Lord, I will surely find better than this as a destination﴾ [al-Kahf: 36], or: ﴿Indeed, with Him there is the best for me﴾ [Fussilat: 50].

Therefore, "the human being" here means the disbeliever, because the Real, glorified is He, wills for the believer to be content (qanu'). This is the contentment that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) taught us when he said to his noble companion, his uncle al-‘Abbas ibn ‘Abd al-Muttalib: [...] And in another hadith the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: [...] And in the sacred hadith: [...]

The Messenger of God (ﷺ) teaches us here the ways of protection from many diseases, and gives us the healing solutions for the economics of peoples. In the past, physicians did not see a connection between shortness of breath and the stomach; they would say: "Breathing is in the lungs, and food is in the stomach." Now they have confirmed that the relationship between them is strong: when the stomach is filled with food, it presses on the diaphragm, constricts the lung, and exhausts the heart.

Hence they found the confirmation of this information in the hadith of our master, the Messenger of God, in which he teaches us how to combine the different necessities of life: food, water and air, and that the believer should not be gluttonous: "The son of Adam has filled no vessel worse than his belly."

We said: if you return from your work hungry, do not wait for the food to ripen; you may find before you remnants of earlier food, a piece of bread, some stalks of rocket and a piece of cheese, and you eat, and you find taste and pleasure in this simple food. Why? Because you ate while hungry, and hunger makes you accept anything and find it palatable.

Therefore the Arab man of sound nature said: "Hunger is the best seasoning," and he said: "The food of the hungry is wholesome, and the bed of the weary is comfortable," meaning restful. Indeed, you find the weary man sleeping his fill, even if he sleeps on pebbles and a mat, while the one who is not weary tosses on his bed sleepless, even if he sleeps on silk. Therefore we say: reflect on Islam, for in it is the solution to our economic problems and our successive crises.

Islam teaches me to be content with what is in my hand, and not to aspire to what is beyond my capacities, for one who looks to what is beyond his capacities is like one who drinks seawater: the more he drinks, the more thirsty he becomes.

Then the Real, glorified is He, completes the picture: ﴿And if evil touches him, he is despairing, desperate﴾ [Fussilat: 49]. If evil afflicts him, (fa-ya'us) is an intensive form of despair, and God forbid. The one in despair is he whose hope and expectation have been cut off. Despair is a quality of the inner feeling, whereas (qanut) is also an intensive form of qani†, and this is a quality of the bodies. They said: because desperation is the effect of despair that appears on the bodies and especially on the face, so you see him dusty, scowling, grim-faced, and God forbid from the state of these people. As for the believer, the marks of righteousness and the light of faith appear on his face; you find him cheerful, pleasant, open-hearted, smiling and joyful.

Then the Real, glorified is He, says:

﴿And if We let him taste mercy from Us...﴾.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 41, verse 50:

His saying: ﴿This is mine﴾ [Fussilat: 50]: "This is my due; I deserve it by my work and my effort." That is, he denies that this comes from God. This is the saying of Qarun: ﴿He said: "I have only been given it on account of knowledge I have"﴾ [al-Qasas: 78]. So God answered him: since you have been given it on knowledge you possess, then guard it with knowledge you possess. ﴿So We caused the earth to swallow him and his home﴾ [al-Qasas: 81].

God spoke the truth when He said: ﴿Indeed, mankind does transgress, when he sees himself self-sufficient﴾ [al-'Alaq: 6-7].

Then he persists in his delusion and says: ﴿And if I am returned to my Lord﴾ [Fussilat: 50], meaning in the Hereafter. The meaning is: supposing there is a resurrection and a reckoning, ﴿I will surely have with Him the best [reward]﴾ [Fussilat: 50], the better recompense. Just as He gave me in this world, He will give me something better than it in the Hereafter.

﴿Then We will inform those who disbelieved of what they did﴾ [Fussilat: 50]. Therefore: informing the evildoer of his evil and making him aware of it is the first stage of punishment. We say to him: you did such and such, and We enumerate his misdeeds upon him as a preparation for calling him to account for them, while he knows that there is no return to set right what lies between him and his Lord.

Therefore the Qur'an relates of them: ﴿[He] says: "My Lord, return me, that I may do righteousness in what I have left behind."﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 99-100]. God answered him: ﴿No! It is only a word he is saying, and behind them is a barrier until the Day they are resurrected﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 100].

And He said: ﴿And if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden﴾ [al-An'am: 28].

As for His saying ﴿And We will surely make them taste a severe punishment﴾ [Fussilat: 50]: "severe" (ghalizh) means intense punishment. Punishment is described by many attributes. Sometimes He says ﴿a painful punishment﴾ [al-Mulk: 28], which causes pain, and ﴿a humiliating punishment﴾ [al-Mujadila: 16], in which there is humiliation and abasement. Among those who are punished, some are suited to, and their crime and nature call for, the painful punishment, while others are affected by the humiliating punishment, which breaks the arrogance of their pride, even if it is not painful.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 41, verse 51:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And when He bestows favour upon man, he turns away and distances himself⁠—﴾ [Fussilat: 51]. That is, he turns away from the Bestower of favours, glory be to Him, because he has taken his need and attained his aim. This attribute is something we find very often in people. A man comes to you seeking help in some matter or some difficulty, and stands at your door morning and evening. But when you have fulfilled his need, he may forget even to say to you "thank you" (shukran).

The poet who depicted this matter did well, when he said:

Those in need walk behind you, humbled,
and if they attain it, they leave you behind and hurry off.

And the best of them is the one who, if you are mentioned with something bad, stays silent, neither denying nor fabricating.

So do not abandon kindness, however much they may deny it, for the reward of God is more pleased and more abundant.

And remember always that those who deny your favour to them are the people most profitable to you, because the one who will take on the repayment of your kindness is God, the Mighty and Majestic. The gift of God is according to the measure of God, and the gift of people is according to the measure of people.

Therefore we see our master Noah, peace be upon him, saying to his people: ﴿O my people, I do not ask you for any wage for it﴾ [Hud: 51]. The meaning: the work I do ought to have earned me a wage from you; yet I do not want my wage from you, but from my Lord, for He is able to give me the recompense and to measure my reward.

And in the context of this verse we notice the gradation in the act of turning away. ﴿He turned away﴾ means he turned his face away. Then ﴿and distanced himself﴾ means he turned his back. So: he turned away with his face, then with his side, then with his back. This same sequence is found in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend them in the way of God⁠—give them tidings of a painful punishment. On the Day they will be heated in the fire of Hell, and their foreheads, their sides and their backs will be branded with them: "This is what you hoarded for yourselves, so taste what you used to hoard."﴾ [al-Tawbah: 34-35].

They said: it was revealed concerning one who rejected the needy petitioner, turning away from him first with his face, then with his side, then with his back. So the recompense is of the same kind as the deed, and according to the measure of the hoarding will be the branding, God forbid.

And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And when harm touches him, he is one of lengthy supplication⁠—﴾ [Fussilat: 51]. Harm touches him merely by touching, ﴿so he is one of supplication﴾ [Fussilat: 51], that is, he is a person of supplication, ﴿lengthy﴾ [Fussilat: 51], continuous. We note that it did not say "long supplication." A thing has length and it has breadth, and length is greater than breadth, yet the Qur'an uses breadth to indicate the greatness of a thing, as in His saying, may He be exalted, describing Paradise: ﴿whose breadth is the heavens and the earth﴾ [Al 'Imran: 133]. If its breadth is the heavens and the earth, which are the widest things we see, then what of its length?

﴿قُلْ﴾ means: say to them, O Muhammad, ﴿أَرَأَيْتُمْ﴾ "Tell me," inform me, and judge for yourselves, ﴿إِن كَانَ مِنْ عِندِ ٱللَّهِ ثُمَّ كَفَرْتُمْ بِهِ﴾ "if it is from Allah and then you disbelieve in it" [Fussilat: 52], meaning: you disbelieve in the Bestower of blessings, ﴿مَنْ أَضَلُّ مِمَّنْ هُوَ فِي شِقَاقٍ بَعِيدٍ﴾ "who is more astray than one who is in far-reaching opposition" [Fussilat: 52]. That is, there is no one more astray than the one who sows discord and opposition between the blessing and the Bestower: he takes the blessing and disbelieves in the Bestower. Here ﴿مَنْ﴾ (man, "who") is interrogative, conveying amazement and denunciation. A blessing requires gratitude to the Bestower and praise of Him.

In other verses, the Exalted, glory be to Him, presents His blessings to us in a generous and merciful manner, and reminds us of them by saying: ﴿وَإِن تَعُدُّواْ نِعْمَتَ ٱللَّهِ لاَ تُحْصُوهَا﴾ "And if you should count the blessings of Allah, you could not enumerate them" [Ibrahim: 34]. The word ﴿إِن﴾ (in, "if") here conveys doubt, because a person does not undertake to count something unless it is likely to be counted, enumerated and restricted. So, supposing you were to set about counting Allah's blessing, you would never be able to enumerate it. He called it "blessing" (ni'mah) in the singular and did not say "blessings" (ni'am), because when you reflect on a single blessing you find within it many blessings.

This verse occurs in two places, but the conclusion of each differs from the other. One is: ﴿وَإِن تَعُدُّواْ نِعْمَتَ ٱللَّهِ لاَ تُحْصُوهَا إِنَّ ٱلإنْسَانَ لَظَلُومٌ كَفَّارٌ﴾ "And if you should count the blessings of Allah, you could not enumerate them. Indeed, mankind is ever a wrongdoer, a great ingrate" [Ibrahim: 34]. The other is: ﴿وَإِن تَعُدُّواْ نِعْمَةَ ٱللَّهِ لاَ تُحْصُوهَآ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَغَفُورٌ رَّحِيمٌ﴾ "And if you should count the blessing of Allah, you could not enumerate it. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful" [al-Nahl: 18].

This is because the elements of bestowal are three: a blessing, a Bestower, and one upon whom the blessing is bestowed. As for the blessing, it is abundant, uncountable and unenumerable. As for the Bestower, He, glory be to Him, is Forgiving and Merciful. As for the one upon whom it is bestowed, he is a wrongdoer and an ingrate.

It is as if your Lord, Mighty and Majestic, is saying to you: O My servant, do not despair of My mercy, and do not turn away from My supplication, however much of a wrongdoer and ingrate you may be, for your Lord is Forgiving and Merciful.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 41, verse 53 (part 1 of 2):

We have said that the sīn in ﴿sanurīhim﴾ (ﷻ "We will show them") indicates the future, so this word will remain applicable until the Day of Resurrection; it will remain true at every time. ﴿āyātinā﴾ (ﷻ "Our signs") means the cosmic signs that point to the power of Allah and the wondrous perfection of His making. ﴿fī l-āfāq﴾ (ﷻ "on the horizons"): the plural of ufq (horizon), which is the extent to which your gaze stretches until the sky meets the earth.
Here al-āfāq means the heavens and the earth. From it comes our saying: "So-and-so's ufq is broad," when he has far-reaching insight into abstract matters. The more insight expands, the more vision expands.
The words of the Exalted, ﴿sanurīhim﴾ ("We will show them"), mean: in the future. Does this mean that Allah the Exalted did not show them His signs in the past? No indeed. He did show them many signs, but they were heedless of them and closed their eyes to them. They overlooked His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And Our word has already preceded to Our servants, the messengers. Indeed they would be those given victory. And indeed, Our soldiers – they will be the predominant.﴾ [al-Ṣāffāt: 171–173].
So this is Allah's sunnah (ﷻ "established way/practice") regarding His messengers and servants, and this is a promise from Allah to support them and make them victorious. The Truthful, glory be to Him, has no partner and no opponent who opposes this promise.
This verse has also taught us the principles of soldiering (jundiyya), and that victory has conditions. Whoever fulfils the conditions of soldiering deserves victory, and whoever violates the conditions of soldiering, then Allah's sunnah must take effect upon him. Therefore we have said: if you see the Muslims have lost a battle, know that they have violated these conditions. And when they are defeated, it should not be said "Islam was defeated." No, rather the Muslims were defeated, those who violated the commander's order and violated the conditions of victory. Defeat must occur to teach them and train them in obedience to the commander's order, because if they had won while in violation of soldiering, the commander's order would have become insignificant to them afterward.
We learned this lesson at Uhud, the day the archers disobeyed the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) by remaining in their elevated positions whatever the outcome of the battle. But they looked to the fleeting goods of this world, and the spoils enticed them when they saw the signs of victory, so they descended and abandoned their positions. Thereupon Khālid ibn al-Walīd encircled and surrounded the army of the Muslims from behind, and the defeat occurred, or at least the victory was not completed. So is it then permissible for us to say "Islam was defeated"?
Therefore we must correct our understanding of this matter. The army of the Muslims may be defeated while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is among them, because they did not take up the means of victory. In that case we do not say "Islam was defeated"; rather the Muslims violated (the conditions) and so deserved defeat. So investigate the causes of the defeat and the causes of backwardness; search for your faults and your violation of the method of Allah, for that is the cause, and history bears witness to this.
At Ḥunayn, they said: "We will not be defeated today through lack of numbers." And who said it? Abū Bakr himself said it, when he saw the Muslims reach ten thousand fighters. When some vanity over numbers entered them, Allah disciplined them and gave them a lesson, so they were defeated at first. But the mercy of their Lord overtook them, restored their morale, and decreed victory for them in the end. ﴿And [recall] the day of Ḥunayn, when your great number pleased you, but it did not avail you at all, and the earth was confining for you with its vastness; then you turned back, retreating. Then Allah sent down His tranquillity upon His Messenger and upon the believers and sent down soldiers you did not see and punished those who disbelieved. And that is the recompense of the disbelievers.﴾ [al-Tawba: 25–26].
So the precursors of defeat that the Muslims witnessed in this war were a kind of training, not hatred from Allah toward His servants, in accordance with the words of the poet:
"So be harsh that they may be restrained, and whoever is discerning [should know that] he sometimes must be harsh toward the one he loves."
So we say: Allah's promise of victory does not fail; rather the Muslims fell short of becoming worthy of fulfilling the promise and of rising to the level of the victory Allah had promised them.
But why do the polytheists obstinately persist in this obstinacy and close their eyes to the signs of Allah while they are clear? They obstinately persist because they were chiefs who had temporal authority, and Islam came to strip them of this lordship, to end this temporal power, and to make people equal like the teeth of a comb: no superiority for an Arab over a non-Arab, nor for a non-Arab over an Arab, except through piety.
So Salmān the Persian, Ṣuhayb the Byzantine (al-Rūmī) and Bilāl the Abyssinian were all, in Islam, nobles and in the front ranks. Therefore the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Lineage belongs to Islam, and kinship is by the religion of Allah." At the time when he made Salmān one of the People of the House, Abū Lahab was a disbeliever cast out from the mercy of Allah!!
We learned this lesson from the story of our master Noah with his son. How eager Noah (peace be upon him) was for the salvation of this son, and how much he supplicated Allah for him! But the Truthful, glory be to Him, teaches him this lesson: ﴿He said, "O Noah, indeed he is not of your family; indeed, he is [one whose] work is other than righteous. So do not ask Me for that about which you have no knowledge. Indeed, I advise you, lest you be among the ignorant."﴾ [Hūd: 46].
So sonship and belonging here are not by lineage and blood, but by religion, by method, and by creed: the sonship of righteous action and following.
The groups that clashed with Islam and fought it were defending their dominance and status in the Arabian Peninsula. Therefore they united and banded together against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and those believers who followed him. We saw this in the blockade they imposed on the Messenger of Allah in the Shi'b (valley), and how they closed off all exits for them and cut off every means of livelihood until they were forced to eat carrion and tree leaves.
Then they tried to kill the Messenger of Allah more than once, and they harmed him with the utmost harm in his person, his family and his companions. But far-fetched for them to reach the Messenger of Allah, for he was under Allah's eye, in His protection and safekeeping. It is as if the Truthful wanted to say to them: beware lest you think that these attempts of yours will obstruct the matter of the call in the Arabian Peninsula. The matter of the call will spread, not in the Peninsula alone, but in all the horizons of the world: ﴿We will show them Our signs on the horizons﴾ [Fuṣṣilat: 53].
The call of Islam was fitted for this spread from several aspects.
The most important: the Arabs were by nature a people of wars and fighting who need no training. Therefore, when the Messenger of Allah wished to fight, he did not establish a military academy nor train anyone in the arts of warfare; rather he found a people ready for fighting, experts in its arts and methods. Each of them, whenever he heard a cry (hay'a) of alarm, would fly to it. That is because the Arab tribes, as you know, were in continuous fighting, and among their wars was one that lasted forty years.
Second: the Arabs were a people of travel and movement, who did not know settlement or stability. The Arab's tent was on the back of a camel, which he pitched wherever he alighted and wherever water and pasture were found. The Arab's non-attachment to a homeland made him ready to travel with Islam through all the horizons of the world and all the regions of the globe.
It was no coincidence that the Prophet (ﷺ) was unlettered among an unlettered nation that knew neither reading nor writing, and had no culture or civilisation. All these qualities, though they would be defects in other nations, were in the nation of Islam and in the Prophet of Islam an honour and a distinction. Had the Arabs been a people of sciences and culture and a people of civilisation and advancement, they would have said of Islam: a civilisational leap.
These are three matters that paved the way for the victory of Islam and its spread in all the horizons of the earth. It is as if Allah the Exalted were saying to the disbelievers, and to whoever opposed the religion of Allah, defied His Messenger, and was heedless of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And Our word has already preceded to Our servants, the messengers. Indeed they would be those given victory. And indeed, Our soldiers – they will be the predominant.﴾ [al-Ṣāffāt: 171–173]: "We will show you other signs which you will not be able to overlook in the victory of Islam and its wandering through the horizons of the earth, east and west."
Therefore He brings us an image that makes us laugh at them and enrages them, where He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Whoever thinks that Allah will not give victory to His Messenger in this world and the Hereafter – let him stretch a rope to the sky, then cut [it off] and see whether his plan removes that which enrages him.﴾ [al-Ḥajj: 15].
That is: let him tie himself with a rope to the sky, then cut this rope so that he falls like one hanged, then look whether his rage departs or not. The meaning is that he will come to an end and die, while his rage will not come to an end.
Look at Islam at the beginning of its affair: how it began and was carried by the weak and the slaves, then followed by the great and the nobles. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went to call the people of al-Ṭā'if, he met from them what he met of harm and mockery, and he found no one to protect him or to take him under his protection except al-Muṭ'im ibn 'Adī, who was a disbeliever; but Allah subjected him to protect His Messenger: ﴿And none knows the soldiers of your Lord except Him﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 31]. Likewise, on the journey of the Hijra, he took 'Abd Allāh ibn Uraygiṭ as a guide on the road, and he too was a disbeliever.
Then he says to them: look at the land of Islam and the land of disbelief. Islam began and set out from Umm al-Qurā and its surroundings, and it now conquers the whole earth from east to west. The land of Islam is growing in extent, and the land of disbelief is diminishing: ﴿Do they not see that We come to the land, reducing it from its outskirts? And Allah judges; there is no repeal of His judgment﴾ [al-Ra'd: 41]. Or have they not taken a lesson from that? ﴿And Allah judges; there is no repeal of His judgment﴾ [al-Ra'd: 41].
So is there, after that, any doubt about Allah's support of His religion? Did this unlettered nation not conquer the two greatest civilisations on the face of the earth at that time, namely the civilisation of Persia in the East and the civilisation of Rome in the West, at one time and in close succession? Indeed, those people had methods of war and arts that the Arabs did not know nor were skilled in, yet they triumphed over them.
They narrate that they used elephants in war, and the Arabs knew nothing about them. But Allah inspired our master Sa'd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ with a stratagem by which he overcame the elephant; he discovered that the elephant's trunk was its point of weakness, so he made special swords with which to strike elephants' trunks so that they fell.
Then Islam entered these lands, east and west, within half a century, and it found that there were supporters and lovers of it, some of whom entered Islam willingly out of conviction, and some of whom found in Islam what they sought, namely Islam's justice and tolerance in contrast to the tyranny of the rulers there and the abundance of injustices and corruption.
All of these are signs that we understand from His saying: ﴿We will show them Our signs on the horizons﴾ [Fuṣṣilat: 53]. The Islamic conquest that spread over the whole world is one of these signs. This wide spread of Islam, you could not repel it, because Allah promised it to His believing servants and promised it to His messengers. And when the Truthful promised the messengers victory, He did not promise them in secret; rather in a Qur'an that is recited until the Day of Resurrection and proclaimed aloud, a Qur'an whose preservation and safeguarding Allah has taken upon Himself. The custom is that you preserve what is yours, not what is against you; but the Truthful preserves His promise, which He guaranteed, because He is certain that it will certainly come to pass.
Among the meanings we understand from the future tense in ﴿We will show them Our signs on the horizons﴾ [Fuṣṣilat: 53] is that the Muslims at the beginning of the affair were oppressed and not commanded to fight, and perhaps some of them died before Allah's promise of victory was fulfilled. When they read: ﴿We will show them Our signs on the horizons﴾ [Fuṣṣilat: 53], they knew that victory was coming even if they died before they saw its joy.
You know that Allah did not command the Muslims to fight until faith had taken hold of their souls and creed had settled in their hearts, to the point that one of them would say to our master the Messenger of Allah: "O Messenger of Allah, is there between me and Paradise only that I fight these people so that they kill me?" The Messenger of Allah would say to him: "Yes." So the man would throw away a date he was chewing and hasten by himself to the battlefield, and hurry towards martyrdom, because of the creed that had settled in his soul, which taught him that he was going to something better than what he was in and was approaching a Paradise whose breadth is the heavens and the earth.
This future sīn in ﴿sanurīhim﴾ will remain, providing us with a gift that does not end until the Hour arrives, which will itself be the greatest sign. We will show them signs at every time, signs in favour of this religion and the support of its people on all the horizons.
As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿and within themselves﴾ [Fuṣṣilat: 53], it means: signs within the selves, within persons, in your flesh and blood and soul, in your organs and parts. In everything within you there is a sign, if you reflect.
Allah the Exalted and Most High created man from clay, and informed us of the manner of creation and its stages. Muḥammad (ﷺ) was not a scholar of anatomy nor did he know embryology; rather his Lord, the Most High, taught him. Modern science came to confirm the truth of what he reported regarding the creation of man from clay, and that his offspring is from a lineage of despised water, and that he was a drop, then a clinging clot, then a lump of flesh, then bones, then He clothed the bones with flesh.
And here science reveals to us every day something new about ourselves and wonders we did not know about ourselves before. When you read the latest of what the sciences have reached concerning the human body, you know that you, in your very self, are a wondrous world and a precise, firm structure. And the one who said it spoke truly:
"You suppose that you are a small body, yet within you the greatest world is folded."
We have previously spoken about some of the wonders of creation, and we said, for example, that the normal body temperature is 37 degrees. You find it is the temperature of one who lives at the equator and the temperature of one who lives at the poles, yet no heat transfer occurs inside the body; you find that each organ keeps for itself the heat that suits it. The liver's temperature is 40 degrees, and the eye does not exceed 36 degrees, though both are in one body, and no heat transfer occurs between them.
Consider the blood, the fluid of life throughout the whole body, and how it keeps for itself a degree of fluidity: if it exceeds it, haemorrhage occurs, and if it falls below it, clotting and paralysis occur, Allah forbid.
Consider the two kidneys and what they contain of secrets, power and marvellous making. If one kidney fails in performing its function, the other performs its task, and the body is sufficient to live with one kidney should the other be lost. For this reason we have said that transplanting a kidney from one person to another is forbidden, because the Creator, glory be to Him, gave us two kidneys, each of which contains a million cells ready to work, of which only a hundred thousand actually work. If these hundred thousand stop, the second hundred thousand follows them, and so on.
So how then does kidney failure occur? They say: it occurs because the hundred thousand have performed their task and then stopped, and the second hundred thousand did not notice in order to carry out their task. So when we take a person's kidney and give it to another person, we say: this is criminal and suicidal, because if the remaining kidney stops, the person must die.
Among the marvels and signs of creation in man, glory be to Him, is the sign of the skin and what it contains of secrets. We understood this from His saying, concerning the punishment of the disbelievers: ﴿Every time their skins are roasted through, We will replace them with other skins that they may taste the punishment﴾ [al-Nisā': 56].
We learn from this verse that the skin is the place of sensation; if it is burned, sensation does not occur. Therefore the Truthful renews their skins for them so that they taste the punishment and the pain continues. The world did not know this matter until after the World War, when the Germans reached the conclusion that the skin is the organ of sensation in the body, as proof of which, when you are given an injection, for example, it hurts only to the extent of the needle's penetration through the layer of skin; after that you feel no pain. So the Qur'an preceded the whole world to this sign.

Among the signs of God within the human self is that you will find inside the body a natural pharmacy (ṣaydaliyya) that treats whatever disorder occurs in the body. We took this from His saying, exalted is He: ﴿from a clot, shaped and unshaped﴾ [al-Hajj: 5]. The shaped (mukhallaqa) is that from which the body was formed with its visible organs and limbs, while the unshaped that exists inside the body serves as a reserve for it, completing what is deficient in it and treating what has fallen ill in it. For this reason, we see that the most modern treatment for wounds and boils, for example, is to leave them to the body's natural resistance, whereby they heal without intervention by harmful chemical substances that leave a mark on the skin.

Contemplate any of your organs and any of the systems of your body. Contemplate how this human being was built in this upright, balanced form, and how he walks, balanced and tall of stature. Contemplate the palm of your hand, with its fingers, and the harmony, proportion and smooth coordination within it.

Look at your digestive or respiratory system. Look at the heart, this muscle that is no larger than a single fist, how it works without ceasing from birth until death. All of these are signs, wonders and secrets indicating the power of the Creator and the wondrous originality of His making, glory be to Him, within the selves.

The bounty of this word ﴿We will show them﴾ (sanurīhim) continues extended through all of time, and every day we witness something new, a sign and a wonder of the creation in the horizons and in the selves. When you survey the Qur'an, you find that it has encompassed in this matter the past, the present and the future. He said: ﴿Do they not see that We come to the land, reducing it from its edges…﴾ [al-Ra'd: 41], and He said of the future: ﴿We will show them Our signs in the horizons and in themselves, until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth﴾ [Fuṣṣilat: 53].

The particle sawfa remains as a future marker, for the distant future. They said: it is for matters of the Hereafter, as in His saying: ﴿So you will come to know who will receive a punishment that will disgrace him and upon whom will descend an enduring punishment﴾ [Hūd: 39].

There is a difference between the futurity of an action from God, exalted is He, and its futurity from human beings. We say: past, present and future. As for the Truth, glory be to Him, all time is equal before Him. Read His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The command of God has come, so do not seek to hasten it﴾ [al-Naḥl: 1], and what is meant here is the Resurrection.

For this reason, the orientalists stopped at this verse, accusing the Qur'an of contradiction: ﴿has come﴾ (atā) indicates the past, and ﴿so do not seek to hasten it﴾ indicates the future. But we must know that the speaker here is God, Mighty and Majestic, who possesses all of time. When He says "has come" (atā), He says it with the full resources of His power and oneness, since there is no opponent to prevent the occurrence of the act. The Resurrection, because it is a reality that will certainly occur, is expressed in the past tense, as though it had already come.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿We will show them﴾ indicates that these signs are distributed across time, such that every generation finds in the Qur'an a new bounty. We now know, of the signs of God in the universe and in the selves, what no one knew in the time of the Messenger of God, although they exist and God informed of them in the Qur'an.

I once asked some of our brothers specialized in economic affairs in the world, I said to them: When did humanity know the elevator (al-asansīr)? They said: in such and such a year, meaning in the twentieth century. I said: Then read His saying: ﴿And were it not that mankind would be one community, We would have made for those who disbelieve in the Most Merciful roofs of silver for their houses and stairways upon which they ascend﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 33]. The stairways (ma'ārij) are what we now know as the elevator.

Likewise the ships and enormous vessels made of decks, which appear on the seas as though they were a moving city, were not in this form in the time of the Prophet (ﷺ). God informed of them in Surat al-Raḥmān: ﴿And His are the ships raised high in the sea like mountains﴾ [al-Raḥmān: 24]. Thus, God, exalted is He, created and knew what would happen to His creation in the future.

If you say: Why did these signs not appear in the time of the Prophet (ﷺ) and of his Companions? They said: Had these cosmic signs appeared contemporaneously with the time of the Prophet and his Companions, the Qur'an would have exhausted its miracles and signs in a single century, and the following centuries would have received the Qur'an without new bounty and without signs that dazzle them and guide them to the power of the Creator, glory be to Him.

God, exalted is He, willed that the reception of the Qur'an by generations remain a renewed reception, such that each generation has a share in the bounty of the Qur'an, to prove to us that He who sent down the Qur'an long ago informed in it of what would happen in the future, and that He, glory be to Him, is one God with no partner who could refute what He has said.

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth﴾ [Fuṣṣilat: 53], meaning: it becomes evident to them that the Qur'an is true and that God is the Truth. The truth (al-ḥaqq) is the established thing that does not change, and its opposite is falsehood (al-bāṭil), which is changing and vanishing. The truth is luminous, and falsehood is confused.

God, exalted is He, depicts for us truth and falsehood in a material, observable example, so He says, glory be to Him: ﴿He sends down water from the sky, so valleys flow according to their measure, and the torrent carries a swelling foam. And from what they heat in the fire seeking an ornament or a commodity is a foam like it. Thus God strikes the example of truth and falsehood. As for the foam, it passes away as scum; but as for that which benefits people, it remains upon the earth﴾ [al-Ra'd: 17].

God is the Truth; what He says is true. Among people are those who recognize the face of the truth in it, and among them are those who doubt and for a period the signs are hidden from them, until events bring them to recognize that it is the Truth from the True God, in fact and in existence.

Falsehood may triumph and rise for a period of time, but the final round must belong to the truth. For this reason they said: "The state of falsehood is an hour, and the state of truth lasts until the Hour arises." The conscious believer who is confident in the victory of God is not troubled by the triumph of falsehood, for it is time-bound, and he awaits the moment when the truth rises and falsehood is vanquished.

The believer knows that when falsehood rises, it becomes a soldier in the army of truth: falsehood reveals the truth to those who do not know it, and the opposite reveals the beauty of its opposite. Had people not suffered from falsehood and been bitten by events, they would not have known the truth nor yearned for it.

Therefore, when you reflect on the Qur'anic order in His saying: ﴿And He made the word of those who disbelieved the lowest, while the word of God is the highest﴾ [al-Tawba: 40], you know that the truth is established, and that it is the principle upon which all the affairs of creation stand. The word of those who disbelieve may rise, but its end is that it becomes the lowest; God made it lowest, so it is a making (ja'l) from God.

As for ﴿and the word of God is the highest﴾ [al-Tawba: 40], you find that "word" (kalima) here is the subject (mubtada'), so it is in its origin highest; it is not a making like the first, meaning it was never lowest, and then God made it highest; it is by its nature highest. Thus we say: falsehood rises for some people through its events, so that they may become alert to the truth.

Then He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Is it not sufficient concerning your Lord that He is, over all things, a Witness?﴾ [Fuṣṣilat: 53]. Yes, it suffices with Him, glory be to Him, as a witness and an observer from whom nothing is hidden. It is as if the Truth, glory be to Him, says to them: It was not proper for you to await signs in order to believe the Messenger; rather you should have believed him the moment he spoke, because God is a witness to him, and God, glory be to Him, has no opponent who could oppose Him and reject His judgment.

For this reason we say: Why did al-Ṣiddīq become al-Ṣiddīq? Because when it was said to him that your companion claims to be a prophet, he did nothing more than say at once: "If he has said it, then he has spoken the truth," without debating the matter. Likewise, when news of the Isrā' and Mi'rāj reached him, he said the same first statement and did not wait until the Qur'an was revealed to inform them of that and then he would believe.

The Qur'an descends to persuade the stubborn disbeliever or the doubting skeptic, whereas al-Ṣiddīq (may God be pleased with him) was at the highest degrees of certainty and faith, and the history of Muhammad's conduct in the past sufficed him; he took from his truthfulness in the past as proof of his truthfulness in the present.

The word ﴿witness﴾ (shahīd) [Fuṣṣilat: 53] here carries the meaning of the witness who establishes the truth, the judge who rules concerning it, and the executor who carries out the rulings.

Al-Sha'rawi, Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66), on surah 41, verse 54:

The word ﴿Alā﴾ (ألا, "Verily" / "Indeed, mark this") is a particle of opening for a new statement. The speaker wishes not to surprise the addressee, so he alerts him so that he will pay attention and not miss anything of what is said. It is as if he were saying to him: "Be ready and listen to what I am about to tell you, for it is an important matter."

The important matter is His saying, exalted be He: ﴿Indeed, they are in doubt about the meeting with their Lord﴾ [Fussilat: 54]. That is: the disbelievers are in doubt about the Resurrection after death. They suppose that the matter is only that God created them in this world and that the matter ends there. Thus they doubt that there is any return, and they are skeptical about the reckoning and the recompense, and they take no account of this Day. Why?

Because they have not prepared anything for this meeting, so they neglect it. A person wishes himself that this speech is a lie, and that there is no resurrection, no reckoning, and no recompense. And whoever among them acknowledges this meeting is filled with conceit, so he says: ﴿And if I am returned to my Lord, I will surely have with Him the best [reward]﴾ [Fussilat: 50]. And another said: ﴿And if I am returned to my Lord, I will surely find better than this as a destination﴾ [al-Kahf: 36].

So they are in (mirya) concerning this Day, that is, in doubt, skepticism and hesitation. The word mirya is also from al-mira' (ٱلْمِرَاء, "disputation"), which is arguing with falsehood, obstinacy, and stubbornness in refusing to accept the truth and submit to it. Therefore they said: jadal (debate, "argumentation") is the discussion that leads to something between two parties, to a conclusion; whereas mira' is a argument in which each party defends itself and does not care to reach the truth.

And Allah, blessed and exalted, teaches us how to disagree, how to discuss, and the principles of debate in His saying: ﴿Say: I admonish you with one thing﴾ [Saba': 46]. What is it, O Lord? ﴿That you stand up for Allah, in pairs and individually, and then reflect: there is no madness in your companion﴾ [Saba': 46]. That is: do not seek the truth through collective, mass discussion, but in pairs and individually, because the judgment of the masses is not disciplined. Each side in it wants to prevail for its opinion, and does not accept being defeated before the crowd, so it persists in falsehood.

We have previously said that in the chanting of the masses the voices get lost and mixed up and cannot be distinguished, and we illustrated this with the verse of Shawqi about Cleopatra when she was defeated at Actium:

Listen to the people, Dayoun, how they are inspired to him,
Filling the air with chants for the life of his killers,
Slander has affected them, and falsehood has been poured over them,
What a parrot, whose mind is in his ears!

The shameful matter here is that they are "in doubt," and He did not say "from the Garden," but ﴿in doubt about the meeting with their Lord﴾ [Fussilat: 54]. This is the great disgrace, the shame and the humiliation, as they said: a situation in which the flesh of the face falls off from shame before the Truth, glorified be He. They have returned to Him in this regrettable return, and they find themselves before the Truth, glorified be He, whom they disbelieved in during the world, denied and rejected. Then this reality surprises them: ﴿And he found Allah with him, so He paid him his account, and Allah is swift in reckoning﴾ [al-Nur: 39].

Indeed, if He had said "in doubt about the bliss of their Lord," it would have been acceptable, since people differ in their ranks and degrees in righteous deeds. Some of them act out of fear of the Fire, some act out of desire for Paradise, and some act out of love for Allah who has obligated them and to please Him, glorified be He, neither out of fear of His Fire nor desire for His Garden, but they act for the sake of Allah Himself.

Therefore it is reported that Sayyida Rabi'a al-Adawiyya said in her supplication to Allah, exalted be He: "O Allah, if You know that I worship You out of desire for Your Garden, then deprive me of it, and if You know that I worship You out of fear of Your Fire, then burn me in it. Rather, I love You because You deserve to be loved." And recite His saying, exalted be He: ﴿So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord, let him do righteous deeds and not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord﴾ [al-Kahf: 110]. And the Garden is one.

His saying, glorified be He: ﴿Verily, He encompasses all things﴾ [Fussilat: 54] confirms another reality, which also begins with the opening particle ﴿Alā﴾ (ألا). The meaning is that His knowledge, glorified be He, encompasses everything with complete encompassing, so that no one escapes it, and no atom's weight is absent from it in the heavens or on the earth. And al-muhit (المحيط, "that which encompasses") is the circle that surrounds a thing from all its sides.
